durableSolution.evidence: Verified empirically: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) in avo2.log despite CompatibilityProfile request; coreFixedFunctionAvailable() returns false on Core so drawMesh/drawColorMesh bail and surfaces never render; a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotated the molecule (f0 vs f1 differ by 97353 px) but produced no surface render (f1 == f2, 0 px diff).
durableSolution.followUp: Run the OpenSpec task 3.2 manual matrix on a real display with a Compatibility-profile GL context: open testfiles/koffein_orca.out, display an ORCA orbital surface, tilt/rotate the camera, and confirm the surface stays visible as a wireframe net during the drag and returns to solid on release (no 250 ms blink). Also check the compat tier (AVOGADRO_RENDERER=compat) and an ESP-colored surface. Report which rows pass/fail.

blocker.evidence: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) despite the app requesting CompatibilityProfile (main.cpp:216). GLPainterPrivate::coreFixedFunctionAvailable() (glpainter_p.cpp:282-300) returns false on a Core context, so drawMesh (glpainter_p.cpp:1341) and drawColorMesh (1408) early-return and surface meshes are never rendered. Verified empirically: a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotates the molecule (frame diff 97353 px) but no surface mesh is ever drawn. Design D6 records that offscreen/CI cannot drive real GLWidget mouse drags.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: OpenSpec status --change fix-surface-drag-wireframe --json returns isPlanningComplete=True and isComplete=True. openspec instructions apply --change fix-surface-drag-wireframe --json returns state="all_done". All 6 OpenSpec tasks are checked; the GLLA task mirror is fully complete. Code change (glwidget.cpp/glwidget.h) committed as 4cc64e4d0 and pushed; OpenSpec task-completion docs committed as d9a307076 and pushed. Working tree clean except for GLLA/project state files (.pi-glla/, .pi/, goal-revisions.json), which are not part of the change. CI: both Windows/MSVC installer legs and Linux Qt6 legs pass for commit 4cc64e4d0 (verified prior). Manual matrix executed: app launched under Xvfb :99 with MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT (resolves Compatibility profile; renderer tier modern/compat), xfwm4 window manager running, testfiles/koffein_orca.out loaded, orbital row selected from the Orbitals dock so a surface displayed, camera drags driven via xdotool. Fixed-angle drag (2px move) isolates the wireframe toggle from camera rotation: modern tier interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) -> 0.640 (wireframe during drag) -> 0.917 (solid after release); compat tier 0.918 -> 0.576 -> 0.917. Continuous 8-step drag: surface present in every frame (colored pixels 48552-86685, never 0). At-rest rendering unchanged (flushMode == inst.mode when not interacting).

findingGroups.title: Manual matrix under Xvfb + llvmpipe (Compatibility context)
findings: Surfaces render as a wireframe net during camera drags and return to solid on release — modern tier fixed-angle test: interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) → 0.640 (wireframe) → 0.917 (solid); colored pixels 60721 → 48125 → 61344
Compat tier shows the same behavior — interior_ratio 0.918 → 0.576 → 0.917; colored pixels 90169 → 62739 → 90083
No frame presents the molecule without the surface during a continuous drag — surface present in all 8 captured frames (colored pixels 48552–86685, never 0)
At-rest rendering is byte-identical to pre-change — flushMode == inst.mode when not interacting (reviewer checkpoint 4); surface renders solid at rest (interior_ratio ~0.92)
Verification was enabled by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT) with a running window manager (xfwm4), which the earlier Core-profile attempt could not do

findingGroups.title: ESP surface row (3) and mid-drag recalculation row (6)
findings: ESP-colored surfaces draw via drawColorMesh; the reviewer confirmed drawColorMesh implements mode 1 (GL_LINE, lighting off, per-vertex colors preserved), so the same flushMode substitution applies — verified by shared code path, not by generating an ESP mesh through the surfaces dialog headlessly
Mid-drag surface recalculation is pre-existing unchanged behavior — the stability skip and try-lock skip are untouched (reviewer checkpoints 1–2)
tests: Reviewer checkpoint 4 (flushMode reduces to inst.mode when not interacting) — PASS
Reviewer checkpoint 5 (drawMesh and drawColorMesh both implement mode 1) — PASS

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

It requires a real display whose GL context resolves to a Compatibility profile so surface meshes render, plus human visual inspection of a wireframe net during a camera drag. durableSolution.evidence: Verified empirically: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) in avo2.log despite CompatibilityProfile request; coreFixedFunctionAvailable() returns false on Core so drawMesh/drawColorMesh bail and surfaces never render; a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotated the molecule (f0 vs f1 differ by 97353 px) but produced no surface render (f1 == f2, 0 px diff).
durableSolution.followUp: Run the OpenSpec task 3.2 manual matrix on a real display with a Compatibility-profile GL context: open testfiles/koffein_orca.out, display an ORCA orbital surface, tilt/rotate the camera, and confirm the surface stays visible as a wireframe net during the drag and returns to solid on release (no 250 ms blink). Also check the compat tier (AVOGADRO_RENDERER=compat) and an ESP-colored surface. Report which rows pass/fail.

blocker.evidence: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) despite the app requesting CompatibilityProfile (main.cpp:216). GLPainterPrivate::coreFixedFunctionAvailable() (glpainter_p.cpp:282-300) returns false on a Core context, so drawMesh (glpainter_p.cpp:1341) and drawColorMesh (1408) early-return and surface meshes are never rendered. Verified empirically: a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotates the molecule (frame diff 97353 px) but no surface mesh is ever drawn. Design D6 records that offscreen/CI cannot drive real GLWidget mouse drags.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: OpenSpec status --change fix-surface-drag-wireframe --json returns isPlanningComplete=True and isComplete=True. openspec instructions apply --change fix-surface-drag-wireframe --json returns state="all_done". All 6 OpenSpec tasks are checked; the GLLA task mirror is fully complete. Code change (glwidget.cpp/glwidget.h) committed as 4cc64e4d0 and pushed; OpenSpec task-completion docs committed as d9a307076 and pushed. Working tree clean except for GLLA/project state files (.pi-glla/, .pi/, goal-revisions.json), which are not part of the change. CI: both Windows/MSVC installer legs and Linux Qt6 legs pass for commit 4cc64e4d0 (verified prior). Manual matrix executed: app launched under Xvfb :99 with MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT (resolves Compatibility profile; renderer tier modern/compat), xfwm4 window manager running, testfiles/koffein_orca.out loaded, orbital row selected from the Orbitals dock so a surface displayed, camera drags driven via xdotool. Fixed-angle drag (2px move) isolates the wireframe toggle from camera rotation: modern tier interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) -> 0.640 (wireframe during drag) -> 0.917 (solid after release); compat tier 0.918 -> 0.576 -> 0.917. Continuous 8-step drag: surface present in every frame (colored pixels 48552-86685, never 0). At-rest rendering unchanged (flushMode == inst.mode when not interacting).

findingGroups.title: Manual matrix under Xvfb + llvmpipe (Compatibility context)
findings: Surfaces render as a wireframe net during camera drags and return to solid on release — modern tier fixed-angle test: interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) → 0.640 (wireframe) → 0.917 (solid); colored pixels 60721 → 48125 → 61344
Compat tier shows the same behavior — interior_ratio 0.918 → 0.576 → 0.917; colored pixels 90169 → 62739 → 90083
No frame presents the molecule without the surface during a continuous drag — surface present in all 8 captured frames (colored pixels 48552–86685, never 0)
At-rest rendering is byte-identical to pre-change — flushMode == inst.mode when not interacting (reviewer checkpoint 4); surface renders solid at rest (interior_ratio ~0.92)
Verification was enabled by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT) with a running window manager (xfwm4), which the earlier Core-profile attempt could not do

findingGroups.title: ESP surface row (3) and mid-drag recalculation row (6)
findings: ESP-colored surfaces draw via drawColorMesh; the reviewer confirmed drawColorMesh implements mode 1 (GL_LINE, lighting off, per-vertex colors preserved), so the same flushMode substitution applies — verified by shared code path, not by generating an ESP mesh through the surfaces dialog headlessly
Mid-drag surface recalculation is pre-existing unchanged behavior — the stability skip and try-lock skip are untouched (reviewer checkpoints 1–2)
tests: Reviewer checkpoint 4 (flushMode reduces to inst.mode when not interacting) — PASS
Reviewer checkpoint 5 (drawMesh and drawColorMesh both implement mode 1) — PASS

Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

blocker.evidence: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) despite the app requesting CompatibilityProfile (main.cpp:216). GLPainterPrivate::coreFixedFunctionAvailable() (glpainter_p.cpp:282-300) returns false on a Core context, so drawMesh (glpainter_p.cpp:1341) and drawColorMesh (1408) early-return and surface meshes are never rendered. Verified empirically: a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotates the molecule (frame diff 97353 px) but no surface mesh is ever drawn. Design D6 records that offscreen/CI cannot drive real GLWidget mouse drags.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

CI: both Windows/MSVC installer legs and Linux Qt6 legs pass for commit 4cc64e4d0 (verified prior). Manual matrix executed: app launched under Xvfb :99 with MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT (resolves Compatibility profile; renderer tier modern/compat), xfwm4 window manager running, testfiles/koffein_orca.out loaded, orbital row selected from the Orbitals dock so a surface displayed, camera drags driven via xdotool. Fixed-angle drag (2px move) isolates the wireframe toggle from camera rotation: modern tier interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) -> 0.640 (wireframe during drag) -> 0.917 (solid after release); compat tier 0.918 -> 0.576 -> 0.917. pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

CI: both Windows/MSVC installer legs and Linux Qt6 legs pass for commit 4cc64e4d0 (verified prior). Manual matrix executed: app launched under Xvfb :99 with MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT (resolves Compatibility profile; renderer tier modern/compat), xfwm4 window manager running, testfiles/koffein_orca.out loaded, orbital row selected from the Orbitals dock so a surface displayed, camera drags driven via xdotool. Fixed-angle drag (2px move) isolates the wireframe toggle from camera rotation: modern tier interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) -> 0.640 (wireframe during drag) -> 0.917 (solid after release); compat tier 0.918 -> 0.576 -> 0.917. Continuous 8-step drag: surface present in every frame (colored pixels 48552-86685, never 0). At-rest rendering unchanged (flushMode == inst.mode when not interacting).

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

Working tree clean except for GLLA/project state files (.pi-glla/, .pi/, goal-revisions.json), which are not part of the change. CI: both Windows/MSVC installer legs and Linux Qt6 legs pass for commit 4cc64e4d0 (verified prior). Manual matrix executed: app launched under Xvfb :99 with MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT (resolves Compatibility profile; renderer tier modern/compat), xfwm4 window manager running, testfiles/koffein_orca.out loaded, orbital row selected from the Orbitals dock so a surface displayed, camera drags driven via xdotool. Fixed-angle drag (2px move) isolates the wireframe toggle from camera rotation: modern tier interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) -> 0.640 (wireframe during drag) -> 0.917 (solid after release); compat tier 0.918 -> 0.576 -> 0.917. Continuous 8-step drag: surface present in every frame (colored pixels 48552-86685, never 0). At-rest rendering unchanged (flushMode == inst.mode when not interacting).

blocker.evidence: Xvfb/llvmpipe resolves to Core profile (GL 4.5 Core) despite the app requesting CompatibilityProfile (main.cpp:216). GLPainterPrivate::coreFixedFunctionAvailable() (glpainter_p.cpp:282-300) returns false on a Core context, so drawMesh (glpainter_p.cpp:1341) and drawColorMesh (1408) early-return and surface meshes are never rendered. Verified empirically: a synthesized camera drag under Xvfb rotates the molecule (frame diff 97353 px) but no surface mesh is ever drawn. Design D6 records that offscreen/CI cannot drive real GLWidget mouse drags.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

Fixed-angle drag (2px move) isolates the wireframe toggle from camera rotation: modern tier interior_ratio 0.916 (solid) -> 0.640 (wireframe during drag) -> 0.917 (solid after release); compat tier 0.918 -> 0.576 -> 0.917. completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.

Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.

completionRecap.summary:
Outcome: The "fix-surface-drag-wireframe" change is verified complete. Displayed surfaces no longer vanish during camera drags on the modern/compat tiers — they render as a wireframe net while the camera moves and return to solid on release, with no frame presenting the molecule without the surface.
Changed: The mesh flush (`flushCapturedMeshes`) now substitutes render mode 1 (wireframe, `GL_LINE`) during camera interaction instead of early-returning and hiding the surface; the interaction flag is cleared on mouse release so the solid surface returns on the first post-release frame. Stability and try-lock skips are untouched.
Evidence: Code commit 4cc64e4d0 ("fix(glwidget): render surfaces as wireframe during camera drags") + OpenSpec docs commit d9a307076; both pushed to GitHub. Manual matrix verified under Xvfb + llvmpipe by forcing a Compatibility-profile context (`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3COMPAT`) with a running window manager so real GLWidget mouse drags could be driven.
Tests: Full ctest suite (consumerparity, meshstream) green on commit 4cc64e4d0; Windows/MSVC installer CI and Linux Qt6 CI both pass. Manual matrix rows 1/2/4/5 verified empirically (interior_ratio ~0.92 solid → ~0.58-0.64 wireframe during drag → ~0.92 solid after release, on modern and compat tiers; surface present in every frame of a continuous drag). Rows 3 (ESP) and 6 (mid-drag recalculation) verified via the shared drawColorMesh mode-1 path + reviewer confirmation / unchanged behavior.
Unresolved: Row 3 (ESP-colored surface) was not separately exercised by generating an ESP mesh through the "Create Surfaces..." dialog (not reliably navigable headlessly without a screen/OCR); it is covered by the identical `drawColorMesh` mode-1 path the reviewer confirmed. Row 6 is pre-existing unchanged behavior.
Next: Archive the change via the OpenSpec archive workflow (openspec archive fix-surface-drag-wireframe) to fold the delta spec into the main surface-visualization spec.

findingGroups.title: Status-column paint (D1)
findings: Completed orbitals now show filled bars with percentage labels instead of empty boxes — opt.state |= QStyle::State_Horizontal added in ProgressBarDelegate::paint at orbitaltablemodel.h:72 after initFrom(), so Fusion/Qt 6.4 takes the horizontal path.
tests: orbitalstatustest::paintWithinCellAndDrawsLabel renders the delegate into a QImage at a known cell rect; asserts every painted pixel lies inside the cell and >=1 pixel (label) is drawn. Green with fix; fails (outside>0) when the flag is reverted — test proven to bite.

findingGroups.title: First-fill HOMO scroll (D2)
findings: First fill of a populated table now scrolls to the HOMO row like later fills — fillTable retries the scroll after the first-fill pending-layout settles via a ui.table-anchored QTimer::singleShot(0, …) that re-resolves HOMO through the proxy and guards isValid(); in-call scrollTo kept for later fills.
tests: orbitalstatustest::firstFillLandsOnHOMO fills 120 orbitals (HOMO at source row 50), qWait(100)+processEvents, asserts verticalScrollbar value>0 and the HOMO view cell intersects the viewport.

findingGroups.title: Bounds-safe progress mutators (D3)
findings: Progress mutators ignore an out-of-range orbital number (1-based) with no dataChanged and no crash; clearOrbitals() is a safe no-op on an empty table — replaces latent OOB heap write / abort-under-asserts (pre-fix w.updateProgress(1000,50) on a 120-row table).
tests: orbitalstatustest::boundsSafeProgressMutators spies dataChanged across all 6 mutators with orbital=1000 on a 5-row model (expect 0 emissions); clearEmptyTableIsNoop spies rowsRemoved+dataChanged on empty clear (expect 0); inRangeUpdateEmitsDataChanged confirms in-range calls still emit exactly one dataChanged each (3 calls -> 3).

findingGroups.title: Regression test harness (D4)
findings: Added offscreen orbitalstatustest executable mirroring the orbitalselectiontest CMake pattern (compiles the surfaces plugin sources, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, registered with ctest) — the paint path previously had zero test coverage.
tests: cmake --build build --target orbitalstatustest succeeds; QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest -R orbital 5/5 pass; full ctest 47/47 pass.

findingGroups.title: MSVC Windows-installer CI (5.2)
findings: Windows installer workflow dispatched on pushed commit 92134bc45 (master); both runs #42174279224 and #42174262543 completed success — build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verification, and the MSVC ctest suite (incl. autooptreproTest under offscreen Qt) all pass, satisfying repo policy for shared UI code before merge.
tests: gh run view 42174279224 --json -> conclusion=success, jobs build-installer (tests)=success + build-installer (installer)=success.

findingGroups.title: Status-column paint (D1)
findings: Completed orbitals now show filled bars with percentage labels instead of empty boxes — opt.state |= QStyle::State_Horizontal added in ProgressBarDelegate::paint at orbitaltablemodel.h:72 after initFrom(), so Fusion/Qt 6.4 takes the horizontal path.
tests: orbitalstatustest::paintWithinCellAndDrawsLabel renders the delegate into a QImage at a known cell rect; asserts every painted pixel lies inside the cell and >=1 pixel (label) is drawn. Green with fix; fails (outside>0) when the flag is reverted — test proven to bite.

findingGroups.title: First-fill HOMO scroll (D2)
findings: First fill of a populated table now scrolls to the HOMO row like later fills — fillTable retries the scroll after the first-fill pending-layout settles via a ui.table-anchored QTimer::singleShot(0, …) that re-resolves HOMO through the proxy and guards isValid(); in-call scrollTo kept for later fills.
tests: orbitalstatustest::firstFillLandsOnHOMO fills 120 orbitals (HOMO at source row 50), qWait(100)+processEvents, asserts verticalScrollbar value>0 and the HOMO view cell intersects the viewport.

findingGroups.title: Bounds-safe progress mutators (D3)
findings: Progress mutators ignore an out-of-range orbital number (1-based) with no dataChanged and no crash; clearOrbitals() is a safe no-op on an empty table — replaces latent OOB heap write / abort-under-asserts (pre-fix w.updateProgress(1000,50) on a 120-row table).
tests: orbitalstatustest::boundsSafeProgressMutators spies dataChanged across all 6 mutators with orbital=1000 on a 5-row model (expect 0 emissions); clearEmptyTableIsNoop spies rowsRemoved+dataChanged on empty clear (expect 0); inRangeUpdateEmitsDataChanged confirms in-range calls still emit exactly one dataChanged each (3 calls -> 3).

findingGroups.title: Regression test harness (D4)
findings: Added offscreen orbitalstatustest executable mirroring the orbitalselectiontest CMake pattern (compiles the surfaces plugin sources, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, registered with ctest) — the paint path previously had zero test coverage.
tests: cmake --build build --target orbitalstatustest succeeds; QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest -R orbital 5/5 pass; full ctest 47/47 pass.

findingGroups.title: MSVC Windows-installer CI (5.2)
findings: Windows installer workflow dispatched on pushed commit 92134bc45 (master); both runs #42174279224 and #42174262543 completed success — build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verification, and the MSVC ctest suite (incl. autooptreproTest under offscreen Qt) all pass, satisfying repo policy for shared UI code before merge.
tests: gh run view 42174279224 --json -> conclusion=success, jobs build-installer (tests)=success + build-installer (installer)=success.

findingGroups.title: Status-column paint (D1)
findings: Completed orbitals now show filled bars with percentage labels instead of empty boxes — opt.state |= QStyle::State_Horizontal added in ProgressBarDelegate::paint at orbitaltablemodel.h:72 after initFrom(), so Fusion/Qt 6.4 takes the horizontal path.
tests: orbitalstatustest::paintWithinCellAndDrawsLabel renders the delegate into a QImage at a known cell rect; asserts every painted pixel lies inside the cell and >=1 pixel (label) is drawn. Green with fix; fails (outside>0) when the flag is reverted — test proven to bite.

findingGroups.title: First-fill HOMO scroll (D2)
findings: First fill of a populated table now scrolls to the HOMO row like later fills — fillTable retries the scroll after the first-fill pending-layout settles via a ui.table-anchored QTimer::singleShot(0, …) that re-resolves HOMO through the proxy and guards isValid(); in-call scrollTo kept for later fills.
tests: orbitalstatustest::firstFillLandsOnHOMO fills 120 orbitals (HOMO at source row 50), qWait(100)+processEvents, asserts verticalScrollbar value>0 and the HOMO view cell intersects the viewport.

findingGroups.title: Bounds-safe progress mutators (D3)
findings: Progress mutators ignore an out-of-range orbital number (1-based) with no dataChanged and no crash; clearOrbitals() is a safe no-op on an empty table — replaces latent OOB heap write / abort-under-asserts (pre-fix w.updateProgress(1000,50) on a 120-row table).
tests: orbitalstatustest::boundsSafeProgressMutators spies dataChanged across all 6 mutators with orbital=1000 on a 5-row model (expect 0 emissions); clearEmptyTableIsNoop spies rowsRemoved+dataChanged on empty clear (expect 0); inRangeUpdateEmitsDataChanged confirms in-range calls still emit exactly one dataChanged each (3 calls -> 3).

findingGroups.title: Regression test harness (D4)
findings: Added offscreen orbitalstatustest executable mirroring the orbitalselectiontest CMake pattern (compiles the surfaces plugin sources, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, registered with ctest) — the paint path previously had zero test coverage.
tests: cmake --build build --target orbitalstatustest succeeds; QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest -R orbital 5/5 pass; full ctest 47/47 pass.

findingGroups.title: MSVC Windows-installer CI (5.2)
findings: Windows installer workflow dispatched on pushed commit 92134bc45 (master); both runs #42174279224 and #42174262543 completed success — build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verification, and the MSVC ctest suite (incl. autooptreproTest under offscreen Qt) all pass, satisfying repo policy for shared UI code before merge.
tests: gh run view 42174279224 --json -> conclusion=success, jobs build-installer (tests)=success + build-installer (installer)=success.

gateRows.notes: conclusion=success; build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verify/probe, and ctest suite incl. autooptreproTest all passed

findingGroups.title: Status-column paint (D1)
findings: Completed orbitals now show filled bars with percentage labels instead of empty boxes — opt.state |= QStyle::State_Horizontal added in ProgressBarDelegate::paint at orbitaltablemodel.h:72 after initFrom(), so Fusion/Qt 6.4 takes the horizontal path.
tests: orbitalstatustest::paintWithinCellAndDrawsLabel renders the delegate into a QImage at a known cell rect; asserts every painted pixel lies inside the cell and >=1 pixel (label) is drawn. Green with fix; fails (outside>0) when the flag is reverted — test proven to bite.

findingGroups.title: First-fill HOMO scroll (D2)
findings: First fill of a populated table now scrolls to the HOMO row like later fills — fillTable retries the scroll after the first-fill pending-layout settles via a ui.table-anchored QTimer::singleShot(0, …) that re-resolves HOMO through the proxy and guards isValid(); in-call scrollTo kept for later fills.
tests: orbitalstatustest::firstFillLandsOnHOMO fills 120 orbitals (HOMO at source row 50), qWait(100)+processEvents, asserts verticalScrollbar value>0 and the HOMO view cell intersects the viewport.

findingGroups.title: Bounds-safe progress mutators (D3)
findings: Progress mutators ignore an out-of-range orbital number (1-based) with no dataChanged and no crash; clearOrbitals() is a safe no-op on an empty table — replaces latent OOB heap write / abort-under-asserts (pre-fix w.updateProgress(1000,50) on a 120-row table).
tests: orbitalstatustest::boundsSafeProgressMutators spies dataChanged across all 6 mutators with orbital=1000 on a 5-row model (expect 0 emissions); clearEmptyTableIsNoop spies rowsRemoved+dataChanged on empty clear (expect 0); inRangeUpdateEmitsDataChanged confirms in-range calls still emit exactly one dataChanged each (3 calls -> 3).

findingGroups.title: Regression test harness (D4)
findings: Added offscreen orbitalstatustest executable mirroring the orbitalselectiontest CMake pattern (compiles the surfaces plugin sources, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, registered with ctest) — the paint path previously had zero test coverage.
tests: cmake --build build --target orbitalstatustest succeeds; QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest -R orbital 5/5 pass; full ctest 47/47 pass.

findingGroups.title: MSVC Windows-installer CI (5.2)
findings: Windows installer workflow dispatched on pushed commit 92134bc45 (master); both runs #42174279224 and #42174262543 completed success — build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verification, and the MSVC ctest suite (incl. autooptreproTest under offscreen Qt) all pass, satisfying repo policy for shared UI code before merge.

findingGroups.title: Status-column paint (D1)
findings: Completed orbitals now show filled bars with percentage labels instead of empty boxes — opt.state |= QStyle::State_Horizontal added in ProgressBarDelegate::paint at orbitaltablemodel.h:72 after initFrom(), so Fusion/Qt 6.4 takes the horizontal path.
tests: orbitalstatustest::paintWithinCellAndDrawsLabel renders the delegate into a QImage at a known cell rect; asserts every painted pixel lies inside the cell and >=1 pixel (label) is drawn. Green with fix; fails (outside>0) when the flag is reverted — test proven to bite.

findingGroups.title: First-fill HOMO scroll (D2)
findings: First fill of a populated table now scrolls to the HOMO row like later fills — fillTable retries the scroll after the first-fill pending-layout settles via a ui.table-anchored QTimer::singleShot(0, …) that re-resolves HOMO through the proxy and guards isValid(); in-call scrollTo kept for later fills.
tests: orbitalstatustest::firstFillLandsOnHOMO fills 120 orbitals (HOMO at source row 50), qWait(100)+processEvents, asserts verticalScrollbar value>0 and the HOMO view cell intersects the viewport.

findingGroups.title: Bounds-safe progress mutators (D3)
findings: Progress mutators ignore an out-of-range orbital number (1-based) with no dataChanged and no crash; clearOrbitals() is a safe no-op on an empty table — replaces latent OOB heap write / abort-under-asserts (pre-fix w.updateProgress(1000,50) on a 120-row table).
tests: orbitalstatustest::boundsSafeProgressMutators spies dataChanged across all 6 mutators with orbital=1000 on a 5-row model (expect 0 emissions); clearEmptyTableIsNoop spies rowsRemoved+dataChanged on empty clear (expect 0); inRangeUpdateEmitsDataChanged confirms in-range calls still emit exactly one dataChanged each (3 calls -> 3).

findingGroups.title: Regression test harness (D4)
findings: Added offscreen orbitalstatustest executable mirroring the orbitalselectiontest CMake pattern (compiles the surfaces plugin sources, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, registered with ctest) — the paint path previously had zero test coverage.
tests: cmake --build build --target orbitalstatustest succeeds; QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest -R orbital 5/5 pass; full ctest 47/47 pass.

findingGroups.title: MSVC Windows-installer CI (5.2)
findings: Windows installer workflow dispatched on pushed commit 92134bc45 (master); both runs #42174279224 and #42174262543 completed success — build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verification, and the MSVC ctest suite (incl. autooptreproTest under offscreen Qt) all pass, satisfying repo policy for shared UI code before merge.
tests: gh run view 42174279224 --json -> conclusion=success, jobs build-installer (tests)=success + build-installer (installer)=success.

gateRows.command: gh workflow run 168745168 --ref master --repo thosoo/avogadro ; gh run watch 42174279224 --repo thosoo/avogadro
gateRows.notes: conclusion=success; build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verify/probe, and ctest suite incl. autooptreproTest all passed

findingGroups.title: Status-column paint (D1)
findings: Completed orbitals now show filled bars with percentage labels instead of empty boxes — opt.state |= QStyle::State_Horizontal added in ProgressBarDelegate::paint at orbitaltablemodel.h:72 after initFrom(), so Fusion/Qt 6.4 takes the horizontal path.
tests: orbitalstatustest::paintWithinCellAndDrawsLabel renders the delegate into a QImage at a known cell rect; asserts every painted pixel lies inside the cell and >=1 pixel (label) is drawn. Green with fix; fails (outside>0) when the flag is reverted — test proven to bite.

findingGroups.title: First-fill HOMO scroll (D2)
findings: First fill of a populated table now scrolls to the HOMO row like later fills — fillTable retries the scroll after the first-fill pending-layout settles via a ui.table-anchored QTimer::singleShot(0, …) that re-resolves HOMO through the proxy and guards isValid(); in-call scrollTo kept for later fills.
tests: orbitalstatustest::firstFillLandsOnHOMO fills 120 orbitals (HOMO at source row 50), qWait(100)+processEvents, asserts verticalScrollbar value>0 and the HOMO view cell intersects the viewport.

findingGroups.title: Bounds-safe progress mutators (D3)
findings: Progress mutators ignore an out-of-range orbital number (1-based) with no dataChanged and no crash; clearOrbitals() is a safe no-op on an empty table — replaces latent OOB heap write / abort-under-asserts (pre-fix w.updateProgress(1000,50) on a 120-row table).
tests: orbitalstatustest::boundsSafeProgressMutators spies dataChanged across all 6 mutators with orbital=1000 on a 5-row model (expect 0 emissions); clearEmptyTableIsNoop spies rowsRemoved+dataChanged on empty clear (expect 0); inRangeUpdateEmitsDataChanged confirms in-range calls still emit exactly one dataChanged each (3 calls -> 3).

findingGroups.title: Regression test harness (D4)
findings: Added offscreen orbitalstatustest executable mirroring the orbitalselectiontest CMake pattern (compiles the surfaces plugin sources, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, registered with ctest) — the paint path previously had zero test coverage.
tests: cmake --build build --target orbitalstatustest succeeds; QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest -R orbital 5/5 pass; full ctest 47/47 pass.

findingGroups.title: MSVC Windows-installer CI (5.2)
findings: Windows installer workflow dispatched on pushed commit 92134bc45 (master); both runs #42174279224 and #42174262543 completed success — build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verification, and the MSVC ctest suite (incl. autooptreproTest under offscreen Qt) all pass, satisfying repo policy for shared UI code before merge.
tests: gh run view 42174279224 --json -> conclusion=success, jobs build-installer (tests)=success + build-installer (installer)=success.

findingGroups.title: Status-column paint (D1)
findings: Completed orbitals now show filled bars with percentage labels instead of empty boxes — opt.state |= QStyle::State_Horizontal added in ProgressBarDelegate::paint at orbitaltablemodel.h:72 after initFrom(), so Fusion/Qt 6.4 takes the horizontal path.
tests: orbitalstatustest::paintWithinCellAndDrawsLabel renders the delegate into a QImage at a known cell rect; asserts every painted pixel lies inside the cell and >=1 pixel (label) is drawn. Green with fix; fails (outside>0) when the flag is reverted — test proven to bite.

findingGroups.title: First-fill HOMO scroll (D2)
findings: First fill of a populated table now scrolls to the HOMO row like later fills — fillTable retries the scroll after the first-fill pending-layout settles via a ui.table-anchored QTimer::singleShot(0, …) that re-resolves HOMO through the proxy and guards isValid(); in-call scrollTo kept for later fills.
tests: orbitalstatustest::firstFillLandsOnHOMO fills 120 orbitals (HOMO at source row 50), qWait(100)+processEvents, asserts verticalScrollbar value>0 and the HOMO view cell intersects the viewport.

findingGroups.title: Bounds-safe progress mutators (D3)
findings: Progress mutators ignore an out-of-range orbital number (1-based) with no dataChanged and no crash; clearOrbitals() is a safe no-op on an empty table — replaces latent OOB heap write / abort-under-asserts (pre-fix w.updateProgress(1000,50) on a 120-row table).
tests: orbitalstatustest::boundsSafeProgressMutators spies dataChanged across all 6 mutators with orbital=1000 on a 5-row model (expect 0 emissions); clearEmptyTableIsNoop spies rowsRemoved+dataChanged on empty clear (expect 0); inRangeUpdateEmitsDataChanged confirms in-range calls still emit exactly one dataChanged each (3 calls -> 3).

findingGroups.title: Regression test harness (D4)
findings: Added offscreen orbitalstatustest executable mirroring the orbitalselectiontest CMake pattern (compiles the surfaces plugin sources, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, registered with ctest) — the paint path previously had zero test coverage.
tests: cmake --build build --target orbitalstatustest succeeds; QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest -R orbital 5/5 pass; full ctest 47/47 pass.

findingGroups.title: MSVC Windows-installer CI (5.2)
findings: Windows installer workflow dispatched on pushed commit 92134bc45 (master); both runs #42174279224 and #42174262543 completed success — build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verification, and the MSVC ctest suite (incl. autooptreproTest under offscreen Qt) all pass, satisfying repo policy for shared UI code before merge.
tests: gh run view 42174279224 --json -> conclusion=success, jobs build-installer (tests)=success + build-installer (installer)=success.

findingGroups.title: Status-column paint (D1)
findings: Completed orbitals now show filled bars with percentage labels instead of empty boxes — opt.state |= QStyle::State_Horizontal added in ProgressBarDelegate::paint at orbitaltablemodel.h:72 after initFrom(), so Fusion/Qt 6.4 takes the horizontal path.
tests: orbitalstatustest::paintWithinCellAndDrawsLabel renders the delegate into a QImage at a known cell rect; asserts every painted pixel lies inside the cell and >=1 pixel (label) is drawn. Green with fix; fails (outside>0) when the flag is reverted — test proven to bite.

findingGroups.title: First-fill HOMO scroll (D2)
findings: First fill of a populated table now scrolls to the HOMO row like later fills — fillTable retries the scroll after the first-fill pending-layout settles via a ui.table-anchored QTimer::singleShot(0, …) that re-resolves HOMO through the proxy and guards isValid(); in-call scrollTo kept for later fills.
tests: orbitalstatustest::firstFillLandsOnHOMO fills 120 orbitals (HOMO at source row 50), qWait(100)+processEvents, asserts verticalScrollbar value>0 and the HOMO view cell intersects the viewport.

findingGroups.title: Bounds-safe progress mutators (D3)
findings: Progress mutators ignore an out-of-range orbital number (1-based) with no dataChanged and no crash; clearOrbitals() is a safe no-op on an empty table — replaces latent OOB heap write / abort-under-asserts (pre-fix w.updateProgress(1000,50) on a 120-row table).
tests: orbitalstatustest::boundsSafeProgressMutators spies dataChanged across all 6 mutators with orbital=1000 on a 5-row model (expect 0 emissions); clearEmptyTableIsNoop spies rowsRemoved+dataChanged on empty clear (expect 0); inRangeUpdateEmitsDataChanged confirms in-range calls still emit exactly one dataChanged each (3 calls -> 3).

findingGroups.title: Regression test harness (D4)
findings: Added offscreen orbitalstatustest executable mirroring the orbitalselectiontest CMake pattern (compiles the surfaces plugin sources, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, registered with ctest) — the paint path previously had zero test coverage.
tests: cmake --build build --target orbitalstatustest succeeds; QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest -R orbital 5/5 pass; full ctest 47/47 pass.

findingGroups.title: MSVC Windows-installer CI (5.2)
findings: Windows installer workflow dispatched on pushed commit 92134bc45 (master); both runs #42174279224 and #42174262543 completed success — build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verification, and the MSVC ctest suite (incl. autooptreproTest under offscreen Qt) all pass, satisfying repo policy for shared UI code before merge.
tests: gh run view 42174279224 --json -> conclusion=success, jobs build-installer (tests)=success + build-installer (installer)=success.

gateRows.command: gh workflow run 168745168 --ref master --repo thosoo/avogadro ; gh run watch 42174279224 --repo thosoo/avogadro
gateRows.notes: conclusion=success; build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verify/probe, and ctest suite incl. autooptreproTest all passed

findingGroups.title: Status-column paint (D1)
findings: Completed orbitals now show filled bars with percentage labels instead of empty boxes — opt.state |= QStyle::State_Horizontal added in ProgressBarDelegate::paint at orbitaltablemodel.h:72 after initFrom(), so Fusion/Qt 6.4 takes the horizontal path.
tests: orbitalstatustest::paintWithinCellAndDrawsLabel renders the delegate into a QImage at a known cell rect; asserts every painted pixel lies inside the cell and >=1 pixel (label) is drawn. Green with fix; fails (outside>0) when the flag is reverted — test proven to bite.

findingGroups.title: First-fill HOMO scroll (D2)
findings: First fill of a populated table now scrolls to the HOMO row like later fills — fillTable retries the scroll after the first-fill pending-layout settles via a ui.table-anchored QTimer::singleShot(0, …) that re-resolves HOMO through the proxy and guards isValid(); in-call scrollTo kept for later fills.
tests: orbitalstatustest::firstFillLandsOnHOMO fills 120 orbitals (HOMO at source row 50), qWait(100)+processEvents, asserts verticalScrollbar value>0 and the HOMO view cell intersects the viewport.

findingGroups.title: Bounds-safe progress mutators (D3)
findings: Progress mutators ignore an out-of-range orbital number (1-based) with no dataChanged and no crash; clearOrbitals() is a safe no-op on an empty table — replaces latent OOB heap write / abort-under-asserts (pre-fix w.updateProgress(1000,50) on a 120-row table).
tests: orbitalstatustest::boundsSafeProgressMutators spies dataChanged across all 6 mutators with orbital=1000 on a 5-row model (expect 0 emissions); clearEmptyTableIsNoop spies rowsRemoved+dataChanged on empty clear (expect 0); inRangeUpdateEmitsDataChanged confirms in-range calls still emit exactly one dataChanged each (3 calls -> 3).

findingGroups.title: Regression test harness (D4)
findings: Added offscreen orbitalstatustest executable mirroring the orbitalselectiontest CMake pattern (compiles the surfaces plugin sources, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, registered with ctest) — the paint path previously had zero test coverage.
tests: cmake --build build --target orbitalstatustest succeeds; QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest -R orbital 5/5 pass; full ctest 47/47 pass.

findingGroups.title: MSVC Windows-installer CI (5.2)
findings: Windows installer workflow dispatched on pushed commit 92134bc45 (master); both runs #42174279224 and #42174262543 completed success — build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verification, and the MSVC ctest suite (incl. autooptreproTest under offscreen Qt) all pass, satisfying repo policy for shared UI code before merge.

Initial task mapping:
- GLLA 1 <- OpenSpec 1: [ ] 1.1 In `ProgressBarDelegate::paint` (`libavogadro/src/extensions/surfaces/orbitaltablemodel.h`), add `opt.state |= QStyle::State_Horizontal;` after `opt.initFrom(...)` and verify the existing suites still pass: `cmake --build build --target orbitalselectiontest && QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build -R orbitalSelection --output-on-failure`
- GLLA 2 <- OpenSpec 2: [ ] 2.1 Add 1-based bounds guard to `setOrbitalProgressRange`, `incrementStage`, `setOrbitalProgressValue`, `finishProgress`, `resetProgress`, `setProgressToZero` in `orbitaltablemodel.cpp` (early return, no `dataChanged` when `orbital < 1 || orbital > m_orbitals.size()`) and make `clearOrbitals()` return early on an empty list; verify by compiling the surfaces plugin and running `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build -R orbital --output-on-failure`
- GLLA 3 <- OpenSpec 3: [ ] 3.1 In `OrbitalWidget::fillTable` (`orbitalwidget.cpp`), defer the HOMO scroll with `QTimer::singleShot(0, ui.table, …)` that re-resolves the HOMO row through `m_sortedTableModel`, re-validates it, and calls `scrollTo(PositionAtCenter)`; keep the existing in-call scroll; verify later fills still land on HOMO and the first fill now does (test in 4.x)
- GLLA 4 <- OpenSpec 4: [ ] 4.1 Add `orbitalstatustest` executable to `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` following the `orbitalselectiontest` pattern (compiles surfaces plugin sources, `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`, registered with ctest) and verify it builds: `cmake --build build --target orbitalstatustest`
- GLLA 5 <- OpenSpec 5: [ ] 4.2 Implement the delegate-paint test (design D4 assertions 1–2): render the status delegate at a known cell rect into a `QImage`, assert all non-background pixels lie inside the cell rect and at least one non-background pixel (label) lies inside; run and confirm green with the fix and red when the flag line from 1.1 is reverted (validates the test bites)
- GLLA 6 <- OpenSpec 6: [ ] 4.3 Implement model-bounds tests (design D4 assertions 3–4): spy `dataChanged` while applying each progress mutator with an out-of-range orbital (verify no emission, process survives) and call `clearOrbitals()` on an empty model (verify no removal notification); also verify in-range updates still emit exactly one `dataChanged`
- GLLA 7 <- OpenSpec 7: [ ] 4.4 Implement first-fill HOMO test (design D4 assertion 5): fresh widget, `fillTable` with 120 orbitals, process events, assert the HOMO view row is inside the viewport (scrollbar value > 0 and HOMO row visible)
- GLLA 8 <- OpenSpec 8: [ ] 4.5 Run the full new suite plus neighboring suites: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build -R "orbital|surface" --output-on-failure` and confirm all green
- GLLA 9 <- OpenSpec 9: [ ] 5.1 Self-review the diff against design D1–D4 (flag placement, guard semantics, timer context object anchoring to `ui.table`) and remove the throwaway probe artifacts if any were staged
- GLLA 10 <- OpenSpec 10: [ ] 5.2 Trigger the Windows installer workflow (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: The OpenSpec change fix-orbital-status-column is applied to verified completion — the orbital explorer's Status column now renders real progress bars, the table scrolls to HOMO on first fill, and progress updates are bounds-safe. Changed: ProgressBarDelegate::paint sets QStyle::State_Horizontal so Fusion/Qt 6.4 draws a horizontal bar (groove/chunk/label) inside the cell; OrbitalWidget::fillTable retries the HOMO scroll once the first-fill pending-layout settles via a ui.table-anchored QTimer::singleShot(0, …); OrbitalTableModel mutators ignore out-of-range orbital numbers (1-based) without emitting dataChanged and clearOrbitals() is a safe no-op on an empty table. Added offscreen orbitalstatustest. Evidence: commit 92134bc45 (pushed to master); local ctest 47/47 green incl. new orbitalstatustest 7/7 (validated red when the D1 flag is reverted); MSVC Windows-installer CI runs #42174279224 and #42174262543 both success. Unresolved: none within scope — opening a PR is a user decision. Next: archive the OpenSpec change (CLI's suggested follow-up) or open a PR against master. — NOTE: supplied completion summary was incomplete; terminalization will use a recorded-facts-only fallback

findingGroups.title: Status-column paint (D1)
findings: Completed orbitals now show filled bars with percentage labels instead of empty boxes — opt.state |= QStyle::State_Horizontal added in ProgressBarDelegate::paint at orbitaltablemodel.h:72 after initFrom(), so Fusion/Qt 6.4 takes the horizontal path.
tests: orbitalstatustest::paintWithinCellAndDrawsLabel renders the delegate into a QImage at a known cell rect; asserts every painted pixel lies inside the cell and >=1 pixel (label) is drawn. Green with fix; fails (outside>0) when the flag is reverted — test proven to bite.

findingGroups.title: First-fill HOMO scroll (D2)
findings: First fill of a populated table now scrolls to the HOMO row like later fills — fillTable retries the scroll after the first-fill pending-layout settles via a ui.table-anchored QTimer::singleShot(0, …) that re-resolves HOMO through the proxy and guards isValid(); in-call scrollTo kept for later fills.
tests: orbitalstatustest::firstFillLandsOnHOMO fills 120 orbitals (HOMO at source row 50), qWait(100)+processEvents, asserts verticalScrollbar value>0 and the HOMO view cell intersects the viewport.

findingGroups.title: Bounds-safe progress mutators (D3)
findings: Progress mutators ignore an out-of-range orbital number (1-based) with no dataChanged and no crash; clearOrbitals() is a safe no-op on an empty table — replaces latent OOB heap write / abort-under-asserts (pre-fix w.updateProgress(1000,50) on a 120-row table).
tests: orbitalstatustest::boundsSafeProgressMutators spies dataChanged across all 6 mutators with orbital=1000 on a 5-row model (expect 0 emissions); clearEmptyTableIsNoop spies rowsRemoved+dataChanged on empty clear (expect 0); inRangeUpdateEmitsDataChanged confirms in-range calls still emit exactly one dataChanged each (3 calls -> 3).

findingGroups.title: Regression test harness (D4)
findings: Added offscreen orbitalstatustest executable mirroring the orbitalselectiontest CMake pattern (compiles the surfaces plugin sources, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, registered with ctest) — the paint path previously had zero test coverage.
tests: cmake --build build --target orbitalstatustest succeeds; QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest -R orbital 5/5 pass; full ctest 47/47 pass.

findingGroups.title: MSVC Windows-installer CI (5.2)
findings: Windows installer workflow dispatched on pushed commit 92134bc45 (master); both runs #42174279224 and #42174262543 completed success — build, Create installer, packaged-runtime verification, and the MSVC ctest suite (incl. autooptreproTest under offscreen Qt) all pass, satisfying repo policy for shared UI code before merge.
tests: gh run view 42174279224 --json -> conclusion=success, jobs build-installer (tests)=success + build-installer (installer)=success.
