tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1.1] Create erasetool.h/cpp skeleton (AVOGADRO_TOOL metadata, eraser icon, tooltip, no shortcut, usefulness below Draw, settings widget with Adjust Hydrogens checkbox default checked) and verify the tools plugin builds
[OpenSpec 1.2] Implement mousePressEvent: record press point in device pixels, begin lasso gesture (clear path, set dragging), lazily connect toolActivated (Qt::UniqueConnection), accept the event
[OpenSpec 1.3] Implement mouseMoveEvent: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept

[OpenSpec 1.4] Implement mouseReleaseEvent release assembly: minimum-path guard (abort on tap), tryLockForWrite (abort cleanly on contention), construct one DeleteAtomDrawCommand per victim inside an UndoSequence (text "Lasso Delete") and return it

[OpenSpec 2.1] Implement screen-space containment in device pixels: project atoms via camera()->project(), bbox-cull, even-odd point-in-polygon, auto-close unclosed path; add pure static pointInPolygon helper

[OpenSpec 3.1] Managed-hydrogen parity: with adjust-hydrogens enabled exclude hydrogens from the victim set and pass adjustHydrogens=true to DeleteAtomDrawCommand; with it disabled every enclosed atom is a victim
[OpenSpec 4.1] Implement toolActivated(Tool*) and null-molecule/changed-document abandon: clear lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); next gesture starts clean

[OpenSpec 4.2] Implement paint(GLWidget*): while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject device-pixel points to world space and draw a closed line loop via painter()->drawLineLoop so it renders on all tiers without painter diagnostics
tasks.verificationContract: overlay renders on real window tier / no diagnostic spam

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 5.1] Add erasetool entry to libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt, create erasetool.qrc referencing an eraser icon (erase.png), verify the tool builds and appears in the palette
[OpenSpec 6.1] Add erasetooltest to libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt (compiles erasetool.cpp + drawcommand.cpp directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest) and verify it builds

[OpenSpec 6.2] Implement containment-deletion test: molecule + GLWidget with known camera, lasso around a methyl group (and unclosed loop), assert enclosed atoms/bonds deleted while outside atoms survive
[OpenSpec 6.3] Implement tap no-op test: press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry
[OpenSpec 6.4] Implement single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes
[OpenSpec 6.5] Implement managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens; with it off, hydrogens deleted as victims
[OpenSpec 6.6] Implement interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via toolActivated) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean
[OpenSpec 6.7] Run the new suite plus neighboring suites and confirm all green

[OpenSpec 7.1] Self-review the diff against design D1-D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove throwaway artifacts
[OpenSpec 7.2] Trigger the Windows installer workflow and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The Erase lasso tool is implemented and verified — press-drag-a-loop-and-release deletes every atom enclosed by the loop in one undo step; taps are inert, managed-hydrogen parity matches the Draw tool, interrupted gestures clean up, release is lock-serialized, and the loop overlay renders above molecule geometry.

Changed: Added libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.{h,cpp,qrc} + erase.png, CMake plugin registration, and a 11-test erasetooltest suite; fixed the overlay depth bug so the lasso composites above atoms instead of behind them.

Evidence: erasetooltest 11/11 offscreen; Qt6 CI 42249894872 success (5/5 jobs); Windows CI 42250370763 success (erasetool.cpp compiled clean under MSVC, 48/48 tests) — both CI gates green on HEAD edf4f96db.

Tests: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/erasetooltest → 11 passed, 0 failed. Both CI workflows green.

Unresolved: Single-click (tap) delete is by design a no-op per spec "A tap never deletes"; the user's report that it "does not work as expected" is this intended behavior, not a bug.

Next: If the user wants click-on-atom delete as a secondary gesture, that's a scope amendment to erase-tool-interaction (+ design note) pending their decision; otherwise open the PR.

The user reported single-click delete "does not work as expected," which is the spec-mandated tap-no-op behavior (requirement "A tap never deletes", scenarios "Tap on an atom"/"Tap on empty space"/"Loop too small to be a loop", enforced by the kMinLassoPath guard and pinned by testTapNoop). tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1.1] Create erasetool.h/cpp skeleton (AVOGADRO_TOOL metadata, eraser icon, tooltip, no shortcut, usefulness below Draw, settings widget with Adjust Hydrogens checkbox default checked) and verify the tools plugin builds

[OpenSpec 2.1] Implement screen-space containment in device pixels: project atoms via camera()->project(), bbox-cull, even-odd point-in-polygon, auto-close unclosed path; add pure static pointInPolygon helper

[OpenSpec 3.1] Managed-hydrogen parity: with adjust-hydrogens enabled exclude hydrogens from the victim set and pass adjustHydrogens=true to DeleteAtomDrawCommand; with it disabled every enclosed atom is a victim
[OpenSpec 4.1] Implement toolActivated(Tool*) and null-molecule/changed-document abandon: clear lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); next gesture starts clean

[OpenSpec 4.2] Implement paint(GLWidget*): while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject device-pixel points to world space and draw a closed line loop via painter()->drawLineLoop so it renders on all tiers without painter diagnostics
tasks.verificationContract: overlay renders on real window tier / no diagnostic spam

[OpenSpec 6.1] Add erasetooltest to libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt (compiles erasetool.cpp + drawcommand.cpp directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest) and verify it builds

[OpenSpec 6.2] Implement containment-deletion test: molecule + GLWidget with known camera, lasso around a methyl group (and unclosed loop), assert enclosed atoms/bonds deleted while outside atoms survive
[OpenSpec 6.3] Implement tap no-op test: press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry
[OpenSpec 6.4] Implement single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes

[OpenSpec 6.7] Run the new suite plus neighboring suites and confirm all green

[OpenSpec 7.1] Self-review the diff against design D1-D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove throwaway artifacts
[OpenSpec 7.2] Trigger the Windows installer workflow and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1.1] Create erasetool.h/cpp skeleton (AVOGADRO_TOOL metadata, eraser icon, tooltip, no shortcut, usefulness below Draw, settings widget with Adjust Hydrogens checkbox default checked) and verify the tools plugin builds
[OpenSpec 1.2] Implement mousePressEvent: record press point in device pixels, begin lasso gesture (clear path, set dragging), lazily connect toolActivated (Qt::UniqueConnection), accept the event
[OpenSpec 1.3] Implement mouseMoveEvent: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept

[OpenSpec 1.4] Implement mouseReleaseEvent release assembly: minimum-path guard (abort on tap), tryLockForWrite (abort cleanly on contention), construct one DeleteAtomDrawCommand per victim inside an UndoSequence (text "Lasso Delete") and return it

[OpenSpec 2.1] Implement screen-space containment in device pixels: project atoms via camera()->project(), bbox-cull, even-odd point-in-polygon, auto-close unclosed path; add pure static pointInPolygon helper

[OpenSpec 3.1] Managed-hydrogen parity: with adjust-hydrogens enabled exclude hydrogens from the victim set and pass adjustHydrogens=true to DeleteAtomDrawCommand; with it disabled every enclosed atom is a victim
[OpenSpec 4.1] Implement toolActivated(Tool*) and null-molecule/changed-document abandon: clear lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); next gesture starts clean

[OpenSpec 4.2] Implement paint(GLWidget*): while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject device-pixel points to world space and draw a closed line loop via painter()->drawLineLoop so it renders on all tiers without painter diagnostics
tasks.verificationContract: overlay renders on real window tier / no diagnostic spam

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 5.1] Add erasetool entry to libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt, create erasetool.qrc referencing an eraser icon (erase.png), verify the tool builds and appears in the palette
[OpenSpec 6.1] Add erasetooltest to libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt (compiles erasetool.cpp + drawcommand.cpp directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest) and verify it builds

[OpenSpec 6.2] Implement containment-deletion test: molecule + GLWidget with known camera, lasso around a methyl group (and unclosed loop), assert enclosed atoms/bonds deleted while outside atoms survive
[OpenSpec 6.3] Implement tap no-op test: press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry
[OpenSpec 6.4] Implement single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes
[OpenSpec 6.5] Implement managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens; with it off, hydrogens deleted as victims
[OpenSpec 6.6] Implement interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via toolActivated) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean
[OpenSpec 6.7] Run the new suite plus neighboring suites and confirm all green

[OpenSpec 7.1] Self-review the diff against design D1-D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove throwaway artifacts
[OpenSpec 7.2] Trigger the Windows installer workflow and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1.1] Create erasetool.h/cpp skeleton (AVOGADRO_TOOL metadata, eraser icon, tooltip, no shortcut, usefulness below Draw, settings widget with Adjust Hydrogens checkbox default checked) and verify the tools plugin builds
[OpenSpec 1.2] Implement mousePressEvent: record press point in device pixels, begin lasso gesture (clear path, set dragging), lazily connect toolActivated (Qt::UniqueConnection), accept the event
[OpenSpec 1.3] Implement mouseMoveEvent: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept

[OpenSpec 1.4] Implement mouseReleaseEvent release assembly: minimum-path guard (abort on tap), tryLockForWrite (abort cleanly on contention), construct one DeleteAtomDrawCommand per victim inside an UndoSequence (text "Lasso Delete") and return it

[OpenSpec 2.1] Implement screen-space containment in device pixels: project atoms via camera()->project(), bbox-cull, even-odd point-in-polygon, auto-close unclosed path; add pure static pointInPolygon helper

[OpenSpec 3.1] Managed-hydrogen parity: with adjust-hydrogens enabled exclude hydrogens from the victim set and pass adjustHydrogens=true to DeleteAtomDrawCommand; with it disabled every enclosed atom is a victim
[OpenSpec 4.1] Implement toolActivated(Tool*) and null-molecule/changed-document abandon: clear lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); next gesture starts clean

[OpenSpec 4.2] Implement paint(GLWidget*): while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject device-pixel points to world space and draw a closed line loop via painter()->drawLineLoop so it renders on all tiers without painter diagnostics
tasks.verificationContract: overlay renders on real window tier / no diagnostic spam

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 5.1] Add erasetool entry to libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt, create erasetool.qrc referencing an eraser icon (erase.png), verify the tool builds and appears in the palette
[OpenSpec 6.1] Add erasetooltest to libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt (compiles erasetool.cpp + drawcommand.cpp directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest) and verify it builds

[OpenSpec 6.2] Implement containment-deletion test: molecule + GLWidget with known camera, lasso around a methyl group (and unclosed loop), assert enclosed atoms/bonds deleted while outside atoms survive
[OpenSpec 6.3] Implement tap no-op test: press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry
[OpenSpec 6.4] Implement single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes
[OpenSpec 6.5] Implement managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens; with it off, hydrogens deleted as victims
[OpenSpec 6.6] Implement interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via toolActivated) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean
[OpenSpec 6.7] Run the new suite plus neighboring suites and confirm all green

[OpenSpec 7.1] Self-review the diff against design D1-D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove throwaway artifacts
[OpenSpec 7.2] Trigger the Windows installer workflow and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The Erase lasso tool is implemented and verified — press-drag-a-loop-and-release deletes every atom enclosed by the loop in one undo step; taps are inert, managed-hydrogen parity matches the Draw tool, interrupted gestures clean up, release is lock-serialized, and the loop overlay renders above molecule geometry.

Changed: Added libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.{h,cpp,qrc} + erase.png, CMake plugin registration, and a 11-test erasetooltest suite; fixed the overlay depth bug so the lasso composites above atoms instead of behind them.

Evidence: erasetooltest 11/11 offscreen; Qt6 CI 42249894872 success (5/5 jobs); Windows CI 42250370763 success (erasetool.cpp compiled clean under MSVC, 48/48 tests) — both CI gates green on HEAD edf4f96db.

Tests: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/erasetooltest → 11 passed, 0 failed. Both CI workflows green.

Next: If the user wants click-on-atom delete as a secondary gesture, that's a scope amendment to erase-tool-interaction (+ design note) pending their decision; otherwise open the PR.

The user reported single-click delete "does not work as expected," which is the spec-mandated tap-no-op behavior (requirement "A tap never deletes", scenarios "Tap on an atom"/"Tap on empty space"/"Loop too small to be a loop", enforced by the kMinLassoPath guard and pinned by testTapNoop). Adding click-to-delete would be a scope amendment to erase-tool-interaction plus a design note replacing/extending D1's rejection of click-delete, with its own regression test — not part of the current add-erase-tool change, so it was left out rather than silently implemented.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1.1] Create erasetool.h/cpp skeleton (AVOGADRO_TOOL metadata, eraser icon, tooltip, no shortcut, usefulness below Draw, settings widget with Adjust Hydrogens checkbox default checked) and verify the tools plugin builds
[OpenSpec 1.2] Implement mousePressEvent: record press point in device pixels, begin lasso gesture (clear path, set dragging), lazily connect toolActivated (Qt::UniqueConnection), accept the event
[OpenSpec 1.3] Implement mouseMoveEvent: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept

[OpenSpec 1.4] Implement mouseReleaseEvent release assembly: minimum-path guard (abort on tap), tryLockForWrite (abort cleanly on contention), construct one DeleteAtomDrawCommand per victim inside an UndoSequence (text "Lasso Delete") and return it

[OpenSpec 2.1] Implement screen-space containment in device pixels: project atoms via camera()->project(), bbox-cull, even-odd point-in-polygon, auto-close unclosed path; add pure static pointInPolygon helper

[OpenSpec 3.1] Managed-hydrogen parity: with adjust-hydrogens enabled exclude hydrogens from the victim set and pass adjustHydrogens=true to DeleteAtomDrawCommand; with it disabled every enclosed atom is a victim
[OpenSpec 4.1] Implement toolActivated(Tool*) and null-molecule/changed-document abandon: clear lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); next gesture starts clean

[OpenSpec 4.2] Implement paint(GLWidget*): while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject device-pixel points to world space and draw a closed line loop via painter()->drawLineLoop so it renders on all tiers without painter diagnostics
tasks.verificationContract: overlay renders on real window tier / no diagnostic spam

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 5.1] Add erasetool entry to libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt, create erasetool.qrc referencing an eraser icon (erase.png), verify the tool builds and appears in the palette
[OpenSpec 6.1] Add erasetooltest to libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt (compiles erasetool.cpp + drawcommand.cpp directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest) and verify it builds

[OpenSpec 6.2] Implement containment-deletion test: molecule + GLWidget with known camera, lasso around a methyl group (and unclosed loop), assert enclosed atoms/bonds deleted while outside atoms survive
[OpenSpec 6.3] Implement tap no-op test: press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry
[OpenSpec 6.4] Implement single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes
[OpenSpec 6.5] Implement managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens; with it off, hydrogens deleted as victims
[OpenSpec 6.6] Implement interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via toolActivated) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean
[OpenSpec 6.7] Run the new suite plus neighboring suites and confirm all green

[OpenSpec 7.1] Self-review the diff against design D1-D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove throwaway artifacts
[OpenSpec 7.2] Trigger the Windows installer workflow and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The Erase lasso tool is implemented and verified — press-drag-a-loop-and-release deletes every atom enclosed by the loop in one undo step; taps are inert, managed-hydrogen parity matches the Draw tool, interrupted gestures clean up, release is lock-serialized, and the loop overlay renders above molecule geometry.

Changed: Added libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.{h,cpp,qrc} + erase.png, CMake plugin registration, and a 11-test erasetooltest suite; fixed the overlay depth bug so the lasso composites above atoms instead of behind them.

Evidence: erasetooltest 11/11 offscreen; Qt6 CI 42249894872 success (5/5 jobs); Windows CI 42250370763 success (erasetool.cpp compiled clean under MSVC, 48/48 tests) — both CI gates green on HEAD edf4f96db.

Tests: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/erasetooltest → 11 passed, 0 failed. Both CI workflows green.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1.1] Create erasetool.h/cpp skeleton (AVOGADRO_TOOL metadata, eraser icon, tooltip, no shortcut, usefulness below Draw, settings widget with Adjust Hydrogens checkbox default checked) and verify the tools plugin builds
[OpenSpec 1.2] Implement mousePressEvent: record press point in device pixels, begin lasso gesture (clear path, set dragging), lazily connect toolActivated (Qt::UniqueConnection), accept the event
[OpenSpec 1.3] Implement mouseMoveEvent: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept

[OpenSpec 1.4] Implement mouseReleaseEvent release assembly: minimum-path guard (abort on tap), tryLockForWrite (abort cleanly on contention), construct one DeleteAtomDrawCommand per victim inside an UndoSequence (text "Lasso Delete") and return it

[OpenSpec 2.1] Implement screen-space containment in device pixels: project atoms via camera()->project(), bbox-cull, even-odd point-in-polygon, auto-close unclosed path; add pure static pointInPolygon helper

[OpenSpec 3.1] Managed-hydrogen parity: with adjust-hydrogens enabled exclude hydrogens from the victim set and pass adjustHydrogens=true to DeleteAtomDrawCommand; with it disabled every enclosed atom is a victim
[OpenSpec 4.1] Implement toolActivated(Tool*) and null-molecule/changed-document abandon: clear lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); next gesture starts clean

[OpenSpec 4.2] Implement paint(GLWidget*): while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject device-pixel points to world space and draw a closed line loop via painter()->drawLineLoop so it renders on all tiers without painter diagnostics
tasks.verificationContract: overlay renders on real window tier / no diagnostic spam

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 5.1] Add erasetool entry to libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt, create erasetool.qrc referencing an eraser icon (erase.png), verify the tool builds and appears in the palette
[OpenSpec 6.1] Add erasetooltest to libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt (compiles erasetool.cpp + drawcommand.cpp directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest) and verify it builds

[OpenSpec 6.2] Implement containment-deletion test: molecule + GLWidget with known camera, lasso around a methyl group (and unclosed loop), assert enclosed atoms/bonds deleted while outside atoms survive
[OpenSpec 6.3] Implement tap no-op test: press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry
[OpenSpec 6.4] Implement single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes
[OpenSpec 6.5] Implement managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens; with it off, hydrogens deleted as victims
[OpenSpec 6.6] Implement interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via toolActivated) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean
[OpenSpec 6.7] Run the new suite plus neighboring suites and confirm all green

[OpenSpec 7.1] Self-review the diff against design D1-D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove throwaway artifacts
[OpenSpec 7.2] Trigger the Windows installer workflow and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1.1] Create erasetool.h/cpp skeleton (AVOGADRO_TOOL metadata, eraser icon, tooltip, no shortcut, usefulness below Draw, settings widget with Adjust Hydrogens checkbox default checked) and verify the tools plugin builds
[OpenSpec 1.2] Implement mousePressEvent: record press point in device pixels, begin lasso gesture (clear path, set dragging), lazily connect toolActivated (Qt::UniqueConnection), accept the event
[OpenSpec 1.3] Implement mouseMoveEvent: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept

[OpenSpec 1.4] Implement mouseReleaseEvent release assembly: minimum-path guard (abort on tap), tryLockForWrite (abort cleanly on contention), construct one DeleteAtomDrawCommand per victim inside an UndoSequence (text "Lasso Delete") and return it

[OpenSpec 2.1] Implement screen-space containment in device pixels: project atoms via camera()->project(), bbox-cull, even-odd point-in-polygon, auto-close unclosed path; add pure static pointInPolygon helper

[OpenSpec 3.1] Managed-hydrogen parity: with adjust-hydrogens enabled exclude hydrogens from the victim set and pass adjustHydrogens=true to DeleteAtomDrawCommand; with it disabled every enclosed atom is a victim
[OpenSpec 4.1] Implement toolActivated(Tool*) and null-molecule/changed-document abandon: clear lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); next gesture starts clean

[OpenSpec 4.2] Implement paint(GLWidget*): while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject device-pixel points to world space and draw a closed line loop via painter()->drawLineLoop so it renders on all tiers without painter diagnostics
tasks.verificationContract: overlay renders on real window tier / no diagnostic spam

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 5.1] Add erasetool entry to libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt, create erasetool.qrc referencing an eraser icon (erase.png), verify the tool builds and appears in the palette
[OpenSpec 6.1] Add erasetooltest to libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt (compiles erasetool.cpp + drawcommand.cpp directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest) and verify it builds

[OpenSpec 6.2] Implement containment-deletion test: molecule + GLWidget with known camera, lasso around a methyl group (and unclosed loop), assert enclosed atoms/bonds deleted while outside atoms survive
[OpenSpec 6.3] Implement tap no-op test: press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry
[OpenSpec 6.4] Implement single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes
[OpenSpec 6.5] Implement managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens; with it off, hydrogens deleted as victims
[OpenSpec 6.6] Implement interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via toolActivated) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean
[OpenSpec 6.7] Run the new suite plus neighboring suites and confirm all green

[OpenSpec 7.1] Self-review the diff against design D1-D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove throwaway artifacts
[OpenSpec 7.2] Trigger the Windows installer workflow and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1.1] Create erasetool.h/cpp skeleton (AVOGADRO_TOOL metadata, eraser icon, tooltip, no shortcut, usefulness below Draw, settings widget with Adjust Hydrogens checkbox default checked) and verify the tools plugin builds
[OpenSpec 1.2] Implement mousePressEvent: record press point in device pixels, begin lasso gesture (clear path, set dragging), lazily connect toolActivated (Qt::UniqueConnection), accept the event
[OpenSpec 1.3] Implement mouseMoveEvent: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept

[OpenSpec 1.4] Implement mouseReleaseEvent release assembly: minimum-path guard (abort on tap), tryLockForWrite (abort cleanly on contention), construct one DeleteAtomDrawCommand per victim inside an UndoSequence (text "Lasso Delete") and return it

[OpenSpec 2.1] Implement screen-space containment in device pixels: project atoms via camera()->project(), bbox-cull, even-odd point-in-polygon, auto-close unclosed path; add pure static pointInPolygon helper

[OpenSpec 3.1] Managed-hydrogen parity: with adjust-hydrogens enabled exclude hydrogens from the victim set and pass adjustHydrogens=true to DeleteAtomDrawCommand; with it disabled every enclosed atom is a victim
[OpenSpec 4.1] Implement toolActivated(Tool*) and null-molecule/changed-document abandon: clear lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); next gesture starts clean

[OpenSpec 4.2] Implement paint(GLWidget*): while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject device-pixel points to world space and draw a closed line loop via painter()->drawLineLoop so it renders on all tiers without painter diagnostics
tasks.verificationContract: overlay renders on real window tier / no diagnostic spam

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 5.1] Add erasetool entry to libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt, create erasetool.qrc referencing an eraser icon (erase.png), verify the tool builds and appears in the palette
[OpenSpec 6.1] Add erasetooltest to libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt (compiles erasetool.cpp + drawcommand.cpp directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest) and verify it builds

[OpenSpec 6.2] Implement containment-deletion test: molecule + GLWidget with known camera, lasso around a methyl group (and unclosed loop), assert enclosed atoms/bonds deleted while outside atoms survive
[OpenSpec 6.3] Implement tap no-op test: press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry
[OpenSpec 6.4] Implement single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes
[OpenSpec 6.5] Implement managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens; with it off, hydrogens deleted as victims
[OpenSpec 6.6] Implement interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via toolActivated) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean
[OpenSpec 6.7] Run the new suite plus neighboring suites and confirm all green

[OpenSpec 7.1] Self-review the diff against design D1-D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove throwaway artifacts
[OpenSpec 7.2] Trigger the Windows installer workflow and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR

pendingCompletion.completionSummary:
Outcome: The Erase lasso tool is implemented and verified — press-drag-a-loop-and-release deletes every atom enclosed by the loop in one undo step; taps are inert, managed-hydrogen parity matches the Draw tool, interrupted gestures clean up, release is lock-serialized, and the loop overlay renders above molecule geometry.

Changed: Added libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.{h,cpp,qrc} + erase.png, CMake plugin registration, and a 11-test erasetooltest suite; fixed the overlay depth bug so the lasso composites above atoms instead of behind them.

Evidence: erasetooltest 11/11 offscreen; Qt6 CI 42249894872 success (5/5 jobs); Windows CI 42250370763 success (erasetool.cpp compiled clean under MSVC, 48/48 tests) — both CI gates green on HEAD edf4f96db.

Tests: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/bin/erasetooltest → 11 passed, 0 failed. Both CI workflows green.

Unresolved: Single-click (tap) delete is by design a no-op per spec "A tap never deletes"; the user's report that it "does not work as expected" is this intended behavior, not a bug.

Next: If the user wants click-on-atom delete as a secondary gesture, that's a scope amendment to erase-tool-interaction (+ design note) pending their decision; otherwise open the PR.

The user reported single-click delete "does not work as expected," which is the spec-mandated tap-no-op behavior (requirement "A tap never deletes", scenarios "Tap on an atom"/"Tap on empty space"/"Loop too small to be a loop", enforced by the kMinLassoPath guard and pinned by testTapNoop). tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Create `libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.h` / `erasetool.cpp`: `EraseTool : public Tool` with `AVOGADRO_TOOL("Erase", tr("Erase"), …)` metadata, constructor (eraser icon `:/erase/erase.png`, tooltip describing the lasso gesture, no keyboard shortcut), `usefulness()` just below Draw, and a `settingsWidget()` with an "Adjust Hydrogens" checkbox (default checked). Verify the tools plugin builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Implement `mousePressEvent`: record the press point in device pixels, begin a lasso gesture (clear the path, set dragging), lazily connect `toolActivated` (`Qt::UniqueConnection`) to abandon an in-flight loop on tool switch, accept the event. Verify it builds.
[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Implement `mouseMoveEvent`: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 4] 1.4 Implement `mouseReleaseEvent` release assembly (D3/D4/D6): apply the minimum-path guard (D4 — abort on a tap, no command/undo/mutation), then acquire the molecule write lock with `tryLockForWrite` (D6 — abort cleanly on contention: discard polyline, no commands, no state), and on success construct one `DeleteAtomDrawCommand` per victim inside an `UndoSequence` (text "Lasso Delete") and return it. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.1 Implement containment in device pixels: project every atom position through `widget->camera()->project()`, bbox-cull against the loop's bounding box, then even-odd point-in-polygon on the survivors; auto-close an unclosed path with a straight segment from end to start. Add a pure static helper `pointInPolygon` so it is unit-testable. Verify via the containment test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 6] 3.1 In the victim set, when adjust-hydrogens is enabled, exclude hydrogens from the victim set; heavy-atom victims pass `adjustHydrogens=true` to `DeleteAtomDrawCommand`. When disabled, every enclosed atom is a victim. Verify via the managed-hydrogen test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 7] 4.1 Implement `toolActivated(Tool*)` and the null-molecule / changed-document abandon: on tool switch, null molecule, or stale document, clear the lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); the next gesture starts clean. Verify via the interrupted-lasso test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 8] 4.2 Implement `paint(GLWidget*)`: while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject the recorded device-pixel points to world space (at the widget-center depth) and draw a closed line loop via `widget->painter()->drawLineLoop(...)`, so the overlay renders on modern/compat/legacy tiers without "painter not active" diagnostics. Verify the overlay renders (run on a real window tier / check no diagnostic spam).

[OpenSpec 9] 5.1 Add the `erasetool` entry to `libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt`, create `erasetool.qrc` referencing an eraser icon (`erase.png`), and verify the tool builds and appears in the palette: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`.

[OpenSpec 10] 6.1 Add `erasetooltest` to `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` following the `selectionsettest`/`drawcommandtest` pattern (compiles `erasetool.cpp` + `drawcommand.cpp` directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest); verify it builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetooltest`.

[OpenSpec 11] 6.2 Implement the containment-deletion test: set up a molecule + GLWidget with a known camera, drive a lasso around a methyl group (and an unclosed loop), and assert enclosed atoms/bonds are deleted while outside atoms survive.
[OpenSpec 12] 6.3 Implement the tap no-op test: a press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry.
[OpenSpec 13] 6.4 Implement the single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes.

[OpenSpec 14] 6.5 Implement the managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens (not as independent victims); with it off, hydrogens are deleted as victims.
[OpenSpec 15] 6.6 Implement the interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via `toolActivated`) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean.
[OpenSpec 16] 6.7 Run the new suite plus neighboring suites: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build -R "erase|draw|molecule|selection" --output-on-failure` and confirm all green.

[OpenSpec 17] 7.1 Self-review the diff against design D1–D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove any throwaway artifacts.

[OpenSpec 18] 7.2 Trigger the Windows installer workflow (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR. Verified: run 42250370763 (Windows Installer on HEAD edf4f96db) completed success — `erasetool.cpp` compiled clean under MSVC in both jobs, Test step reported 100% tests passed (48/48).

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Create `libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.h` / `erasetool.cpp`: `EraseTool : public Tool` with `AVOGADRO_TOOL("Erase", tr("Erase"), …)` metadata, constructor (eraser icon `:/erase/erase.png`, tooltip describing the lasso gesture, no keyboard shortcut), `usefulness()` just below Draw, and a `settingsWidget()` with an "Adjust Hydrogens" checkbox (default checked). Verify the tools plugin builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Implement `mousePressEvent`: record the press point in device pixels, begin a lasso gesture (clear the path, set dragging), lazily connect `toolActivated` (`Qt::UniqueConnection`) to abandon an in-flight loop on tool switch, accept the event. Verify it builds.
[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Implement `mouseMoveEvent`: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 4] 1.4 Implement `mouseReleaseEvent` release assembly (D3/D4/D6): apply the minimum-path guard (D4 — abort on a tap, no command/undo/mutation), then acquire the molecule write lock with `tryLockForWrite` (D6 — abort cleanly on contention: discard polyline, no commands, no state), and on success construct one `DeleteAtomDrawCommand` per victim inside an `UndoSequence` (text "Lasso Delete") and return it. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.1 Implement containment in device pixels: project every atom position through `widget->camera()->project()`, bbox-cull against the loop's bounding box, then even-odd point-in-polygon on the survivors; auto-close an unclosed path with a straight segment from end to start. Add a pure static helper `pointInPolygon` so it is unit-testable. Verify via the containment test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 6] 3.1 In the victim set, when adjust-hydrogens is enabled, exclude hydrogens from the victim set; heavy-atom victims pass `adjustHydrogens=true` to `DeleteAtomDrawCommand`. When disabled, every enclosed atom is a victim. Verify via the managed-hydrogen test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 7] 4.1 Implement `toolActivated(Tool*)` and the null-molecule / changed-document abandon: on tool switch, null molecule, or stale document, clear the lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); the next gesture starts clean. Verify via the interrupted-lasso test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 8] 4.2 Implement `paint(GLWidget*)`: while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject the recorded device-pixel points to world space (at the widget-center depth) and draw a closed line loop via `widget->painter()->drawLineLoop(...)`, so the overlay renders on modern/compat/legacy tiers without "painter not active" diagnostics. Verify the overlay renders (run on a real window tier / check no diagnostic spam).

[OpenSpec 9] 5.1 Add the `erasetool` entry to `libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt`, create `erasetool.qrc` referencing an eraser icon (`erase.png`), and verify the tool builds and appears in the palette: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`.

[OpenSpec 10] 6.1 Add `erasetooltest` to `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` following the `selectionsettest`/`drawcommandtest` pattern (compiles `erasetool.cpp` + `drawcommand.cpp` directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest); verify it builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetooltest`.

[OpenSpec 11] 6.2 Implement the containment-deletion test: set up a molecule + GLWidget with a known camera, drive a lasso around a methyl group (and an unclosed loop), and assert enclosed atoms/bonds are deleted while outside atoms survive.
[OpenSpec 12] 6.3 Implement the tap no-op test: a press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry.
[OpenSpec 13] 6.4 Implement the single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes.

[OpenSpec 14] 6.5 Implement the managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens (not as independent victims); with it off, hydrogens are deleted as victims.
[OpenSpec 15] 6.6 Implement the interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via `toolActivated`) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean.
[OpenSpec 16] 6.7 Run the new suite plus neighboring suites: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build -R "erase|draw|molecule|selection" --output-on-failure` and confirm all green.

[OpenSpec 17] 7.1 Self-review the diff against design D1–D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove any throwaway artifacts.

[OpenSpec 18] 7.2 Trigger the Windows installer workflow (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR. Verified: run 42250370763 (Windows Installer on HEAD edf4f96db) completed success — `erasetool.cpp` compiled clean under MSVC in both jobs, Test step reported 100% tests passed (48/48).

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Create `libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.h` / `erasetool.cpp`: `EraseTool : public Tool` with `AVOGADRO_TOOL("Erase", tr("Erase"), …)` metadata, constructor (eraser icon `:/erase/erase.png`, tooltip describing the lasso gesture, no keyboard shortcut), `usefulness()` just below Draw, and a `settingsWidget()` with an "Adjust Hydrogens" checkbox (default checked). Verify the tools plugin builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Implement `mousePressEvent`: record the press point in device pixels, begin a lasso gesture (clear the path, set dragging), lazily connect `toolActivated` (`Qt::UniqueConnection`) to abandon an in-flight loop on tool switch, accept the event. Verify it builds.
[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Implement `mouseMoveEvent`: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 4] 1.4 Implement `mouseReleaseEvent` release assembly (D3/D4/D6/D10): apply the minimum-path guard (D4 — route a sub-threshold press-release to a click and a longer drag to a lasso), then acquire the molecule write lock with `tryLockForWrite` (D6 — abort cleanly on contention: discard polyline, no commands, no state), and on success assemble the deletion — a single `DeleteAtomDrawCommand` for a click (D10) or one command per victim inside an `UndoSequence` for a lasso (D3), text "Lasso Delete" — and return it. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.1 Implement containment in device pixels: project every atom position through `widget->camera()->project()`, bbox-cull against the loop's bounding box, then even-odd point-in-polygon on the survivors; auto-close an unclosed path with a straight segment from end to start. Add a pure static helper `pointInPolygon` so it is unit-testable. Verify via the containment test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 6] 3.1 In the victim set, when adjust-hydrogens is enabled, exclude hydrogens from the victim set; heavy-atom victims pass `adjustHydrogens=true` to `DeleteAtomDrawCommand`. When disabled, every enclosed atom is a victim. Verify via the managed-hydrogen test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 7] 4.1 Implement `toolActivated(Tool*)` and the null-molecule / changed-document abandon: on tool switch, null molecule, or stale document, clear the lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); the next gesture starts clean. Verify via the interrupted-lasso test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 8] 4.2 Implement `paint(GLWidget*)`: while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject the recorded device-pixel points to world space (at the widget-center depth) and draw a closed line loop via `widget->painter()->drawLineLoop(...)`, so the overlay renders on modern/compat/legacy tiers without "painter not active" diagnostics. Verify the overlay renders (run on a real window tier / check no diagnostic spam).

[OpenSpec 9] 5.1 Add the `erasetool` entry to `libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt`, create `erasetool.qrc` referencing an eraser icon (`erase.png`), and verify the tool builds and appears in the palette: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`.

[OpenSpec 10] 6.1 Add `erasetooltest` to `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` following the `selectionsettest`/`drawcommandtest` pattern (compiles `erasetool.cpp` + `drawcommand.cpp` directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest); verify it builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetooltest`.

[OpenSpec 11] 6.2 Implement the containment-deletion test: set up a molecule + GLWidget with a known camera, drive a lasso around a methyl group (and an unclosed loop), and assert enclosed atoms/bonds are deleted while outside atoms survive.
[OpenSpec 12] 6.3 Implement the tap no-op test: a press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry.
[OpenSpec 13] 6.4 Implement the single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes.

[OpenSpec 14] 6.5 Implement the managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens (not as independent victims); with it off, hydrogens are deleted as victims.
[OpenSpec 15] 6.6 Implement the interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via `toolActivated`) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean.
[OpenSpec 16] 6.7 Run the new suite plus neighboring suites: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build -R "erase|draw|molecule|selection" --output-on-failure` and confirm all green.

[OpenSpec 17] 7.1 Self-review the diff against design D1–D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove any throwaway artifacts.

[OpenSpec 18] 7.2 Trigger the Windows installer workflow (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR. Verified: run 42250370763 (Windows Installer on HEAD edf4f96db) completed success — `erasetool.cpp` compiled clean under MSVC in both jobs, Test step reported 100% tests passed (48/48).
[OpenSpec 19] 8.1 At `mouseReleaseEvent`, branch on the minimum-path guard: a
[OpenSpec 20] 8.2 Implement the click single-atom deletion test: click on an atom
[OpenSpec 21] 8.3 Update the tap no-op test (6.3) to a click test: a sub-threshold
[OpenSpec 22] 8.4 Re-run the erase suite plus neighboring suites and confirm all green.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Create `libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.h` / `erasetool.cpp`: `EraseTool : public Tool` with `AVOGADRO_TOOL("Erase", tr("Erase"), …)` metadata, constructor (eraser icon `:/erase/erase.png`, tooltip describing the lasso gesture, no keyboard shortcut), `usefulness()` just below Draw, and a `settingsWidget()` with an "Adjust Hydrogens" checkbox (default checked). Verify the tools plugin builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Implement `mousePressEvent`: record the press point in device pixels, begin a lasso gesture (clear the path, set dragging), lazily connect `toolActivated` (`Qt::UniqueConnection`) to abandon an in-flight loop on tool switch, accept the event. Verify it builds.
[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Implement `mouseMoveEvent`: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 4] 1.4 Implement `mouseReleaseEvent` release assembly (D3/D4/D6/D10): apply the minimum-path guard (D4 — route a sub-threshold press-release to a click and a longer drag to a lasso), then acquire the molecule write lock with `tryLockForWrite` (D6 — abort cleanly on contention: discard polyline, no commands, no state), and on success assemble the deletion — a single `DeleteAtomDrawCommand` for a click (D10) or one command per victim inside an `UndoSequence` for a lasso (D3), text "Lasso Delete" — and return it. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.1 Implement containment in device pixels: project every atom position through `widget->camera()->project()`, bbox-cull against the loop's bounding box, then even-odd point-in-polygon on the survivors; auto-close an unclosed path with a straight segment from end to start. Add a pure static helper `pointInPolygon` so it is unit-testable. Verify via the containment test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 6] 3.1 In the victim set, when adjust-hydrogens is enabled, exclude hydrogens from the victim set; heavy-atom victims pass `adjustHydrogens=true` to `DeleteAtomDrawCommand`. When disabled, every enclosed atom is a victim. Verify via the managed-hydrogen test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 7] 4.1 Implement `toolActivated(Tool*)` and the null-molecule / changed-document abandon: on tool switch, null molecule, or stale document, clear the lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); the next gesture starts clean. Verify via the interrupted-lasso test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 8] 4.2 Implement `paint(GLWidget*)`: while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject the recorded device-pixel points to world space (at the widget-center depth) and draw a closed line loop via `widget->painter()->drawLineLoop(...)`, so the overlay renders on modern/compat/legacy tiers without "painter not active" diagnostics. Verify the overlay renders (run on a real window tier / check no diagnostic spam).

[OpenSpec 9] 5.1 Add the `erasetool` entry to `libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt`, create `erasetool.qrc` referencing an eraser icon (`erase.png`), and verify the tool builds and appears in the palette: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`.

[OpenSpec 10] 6.1 Add `erasetooltest` to `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` following the `selectionsettest`/`drawcommandtest` pattern (compiles `erasetool.cpp` + `drawcommand.cpp` directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest); verify it builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetooltest`.

[OpenSpec 11] 6.2 Implement the containment-deletion test: set up a molecule + GLWidget with a known camera, drive a lasso around a methyl group (and an unclosed loop), and assert enclosed atoms/bonds are deleted while outside atoms survive.
[OpenSpec 12] 6.3 Implement the tap no-op test: a press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry.
[OpenSpec 13] 6.4 Implement the single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes.

[OpenSpec 14] 6.5 Implement the managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens (not as independent victims); with it off, hydrogens are deleted as victims.
[OpenSpec 15] 6.6 Implement the interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via `toolActivated`) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean.
[OpenSpec 16] 6.7 Run the new suite plus neighboring suites: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build -R "erase|draw|molecule|selection" --output-on-failure` and confirm all green.

[OpenSpec 17] 7.1 Self-review the diff against design D1–D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove any throwaway artifacts.

[OpenSpec 18] 7.2 Trigger the Windows installer workflow (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR. Verified: run 42250370763 (Windows Installer on HEAD edf4f96db) completed success — `erasetool.cpp` compiled clean under MSVC in both jobs, Test step reported 100% tests passed (48/48).
[OpenSpec 19] 8.1 At `mouseReleaseEvent`, branch on the minimum-path guard: a
[OpenSpec 20] 8.2 Implement the click single-atom deletion test: click on an atom
[OpenSpec 21] 8.3 Update the tap no-op test (6.3) to a click test: a sub-threshold
[OpenSpec 22] 8.4 Re-run the erase suite plus neighboring suites and confirm all green.

findingGroups.title: Click-delete implementation
findings: Erase tool now offers two gestures: lasso group-delete and single-click single-atom delete, routed by the minimum-path guard at mouseReleaseEvent — a sub-threshold press-release clicks (deletes the nearest atom within pick radius via screen-space camera projection, no GL_SELECT), a longer drag lassos. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp handleClick/nearestAtomAt; erasetooltest testClickSingleAtom/testClickResolvesNearestAtom/testClickEmptySpace

Click and lasso deletions take the molecule write lock at release (tryLockForWrite) and abort cleanly on contention; a click is one DeleteAtomDrawCommand, a lasso is an UndoSequence of them, so each gesture is exactly one undo step with nothing mutated before release. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp mouseReleaseEvent; erasetooltest testSingleUndo

Managed-hydrogen parity with the Draw tool: with adjust-hydrogens on, a click/lasso deletes only heavy atoms and lets the delete churn managed hydrogens; with it off, enclosed/explicit hydrogens are deleted as victims, ordered first so undo restores the heavy atom before hydrogen bonds re-add. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp; erasetooltest testClickManagedHydrogenParity testManagedHydrogenParity

findingGroups.title: MSVC portability fix (caught by CI)
findings: The first Windows CI run failed to compile erasetooltest.cpp: `near` and `far` are MSVC far/near pointer-qualifier keywords, so `Atom *near`/`Atom *far` locals produced C2059. Renamed them to nearAtom/farAtom — a behavior-preserving rename; GCC treats them as ordinary identifiers. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp:358-361,379-380; confirmed by CI run 42356674345 passing where 42352599611 failed

findingGroups.title: Test coverage
findings: erasetooltest covers containment deletion, single-undo, managed-hydrogen parity, interrupted-lasso cleanup, lock-contention abort, overlay paint, point-in-polygon, plus the four click scenarios (single atom, empty space, nearest resolution, hydrogen parity) — 14/14 green under xvfb. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp

findingGroups.title: Click-delete implementation
findings: Erase tool now offers two gestures: lasso group-delete and single-click single-atom delete, routed by the minimum-path guard at mouseReleaseEvent — a sub-threshold press-release clicks (deletes the nearest atom within pick radius via screen-space camera projection, no GL_SELECT), a longer drag lassos. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp handleClick/nearestAtomAt; erasetooltest testClickSingleAtom/testClickResolvesNearestAtom/testClickEmptySpace

Click and lasso deletions take the molecule write lock at release (tryLockForWrite) and abort cleanly on contention; a click is one DeleteAtomDrawCommand, a lasso is an UndoSequence of them, so each gesture is exactly one undo step with nothing mutated before release. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp mouseReleaseEvent; erasetooltest testSingleUndo

Managed-hydrogen parity with the Draw tool: with adjust-hydrogens on, a click/lasso deletes only heavy atoms and lets the delete churn managed hydrogens; with it off, enclosed/explicit hydrogens are deleted as victims, ordered first so undo restores the heavy atom before hydrogen bonds re-add. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp; erasetooltest testClickManagedHydrogenParity testManagedHydrogenParity

findingGroups.title: MSVC portability fix (caught by CI)
findings: The first Windows CI run failed to compile erasetooltest.cpp: `near` and `far` are MSVC far/near pointer-qualifier keywords, so `Atom *near`/`Atom *far` locals produced C2059. Renamed them to nearAtom/farAtom — a behavior-preserving rename; GCC treats them as ordinary identifiers. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp:358-361,379-380; confirmed by CI run 42356674345 passing where 42352599611 failed

findingGroups.title: Test coverage
findings: erasetooltest covers containment deletion, single-undo, managed-hydrogen parity, interrupted-lasso cleanup, lock-contention abort, overlay paint, point-in-polygon, plus the four click scenarios (single atom, empty space, nearest resolution, hydrogen parity) — 14/14 green under xvfb. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Create `libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.h` / `erasetool.cpp`: `EraseTool : public Tool` with `AVOGADRO_TOOL("Erase", tr("Erase"), …)` metadata, constructor (eraser icon `:/erase/erase.png`, tooltip describing the lasso gesture, no keyboard shortcut), `usefulness()` just below Draw, and a `settingsWidget()` with an "Adjust Hydrogens" checkbox (default checked). Verify the tools plugin builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Implement `mousePressEvent`: record the press point in device pixels, begin a lasso gesture (clear the path, set dragging), lazily connect `toolActivated` (`Qt::UniqueConnection`) to abandon an in-flight loop on tool switch, accept the event. Verify it builds.
[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Implement `mouseMoveEvent`: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 4] 1.4 Implement `mouseReleaseEvent` release assembly (D3/D4/D6/D10): apply the minimum-path guard (D4 — route a sub-threshold press-release to a click and a longer drag to a lasso), then acquire the molecule write lock with `tryLockForWrite` (D6 — abort cleanly on contention: discard polyline, no commands, no state), and on success assemble the deletion — a single `DeleteAtomDrawCommand` for a click (D10) or one command per victim inside an `UndoSequence` for a lasso (D3), text "Lasso Delete" — and return it. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.1 Implement containment in device pixels: project every atom position through `widget->camera()->project()`, bbox-cull against the loop's bounding box, then even-odd point-in-polygon on the survivors; auto-close an unclosed path with a straight segment from end to start. Add a pure static helper `pointInPolygon` so it is unit-testable. Verify via the containment test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 6] 3.1 In the victim set, when adjust-hydrogens is enabled, exclude hydrogens from the victim set; heavy-atom victims pass `adjustHydrogens=true` to `DeleteAtomDrawCommand`. When disabled, every enclosed atom is a victim. Verify via the managed-hydrogen test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 7] 4.1 Implement `toolActivated(Tool*)` and the null-molecule / changed-document abandon: on tool switch, null molecule, or stale document, clear the lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); the next gesture starts clean. Verify via the interrupted-lasso test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 8] 4.2 Implement `paint(GLWidget*)`: while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject the recorded device-pixel points to world space (at the widget-center depth) and draw a closed line loop via `widget->painter()->drawLineLoop(...)`, so the overlay renders on modern/compat/legacy tiers without "painter not active" diagnostics. Verify the overlay renders (run on a real window tier / check no diagnostic spam).

[OpenSpec 9] 5.1 Add the `erasetool` entry to `libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt`, create `erasetool.qrc` referencing an eraser icon (`erase.png`), and verify the tool builds and appears in the palette: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`.

[OpenSpec 10] 6.1 Add `erasetooltest` to `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` following the `selectionsettest`/`drawcommandtest` pattern (compiles `erasetool.cpp` + `drawcommand.cpp` directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest); verify it builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetooltest`.

[OpenSpec 11] 6.2 Implement the containment-deletion test: set up a molecule + GLWidget with a known camera, drive a lasso around a methyl group (and an unclosed loop), and assert enclosed atoms/bonds are deleted while outside atoms survive.
[OpenSpec 12] 6.3 Implement the tap no-op test: a press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry.
[OpenSpec 13] 6.4 Implement the single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes.

[OpenSpec 14] 6.5 Implement the managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens (not as independent victims); with it off, hydrogens are deleted as victims.
[OpenSpec 15] 6.6 Implement the interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via `toolActivated`) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean.
[OpenSpec 16] 6.7 Run the new suite plus neighboring suites: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build -R "erase|draw|molecule|selection" --output-on-failure` and confirm all green.

[OpenSpec 17] 7.1 Self-review the diff against design D1–D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove any throwaway artifacts.

[OpenSpec 18] 7.2 Trigger the Windows installer workflow (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR. [OpenSpec 20] 8.2 Implement the click single-atom deletion test: click on an atom

findingGroups.title: Click-delete implementation
findings: Erase tool now offers two gestures: lasso group-delete and single-click single-atom delete, routed by the minimum-path guard at mouseReleaseEvent — a sub-threshold press-release clicks (deletes the nearest atom within pick radius via screen-space camera projection, no GL_SELECT), a longer drag lassos. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp handleClick/nearestAtomAt; erasetooltest testClickSingleAtom/testClickResolvesNearestAtom/testClickEmptySpace

Click and lasso deletions take the molecule write lock at release (tryLockForWrite) and abort cleanly on contention; a click is one DeleteAtomDrawCommand, a lasso is an UndoSequence of them, so each gesture is exactly one undo step with nothing mutated before release. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp mouseReleaseEvent; erasetooltest testSingleUndo

Managed-hydrogen parity with the Draw tool: with adjust-hydrogens on, a click/lasso deletes only heavy atoms and lets the delete churn managed hydrogens; with it off, enclosed/explicit hydrogens are deleted as victims, ordered first so undo restores the heavy atom before hydrogen bonds re-add. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp; erasetooltest testClickManagedHydrogenParity testManagedHydrogenParity

findingGroups.title: MSVC portability fix (caught by CI)
findings: The first Windows CI run failed to compile erasetooltest.cpp: `near` and `far` are MSVC far/near pointer-qualifier keywords, so `Atom *near`/`Atom *far` locals produced C2059. Renamed them to nearAtom/farAtom — a behavior-preserving rename; GCC treats them as ordinary identifiers. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp:358-361,379-380; confirmed by CI run 42356674345 passing where 42352599611 failed

findingGroups.title: Test coverage
findings: erasetooltest covers containment deletion, single-undo, managed-hydrogen parity, interrupted-lasso cleanup, lock-contention abort, overlay paint, point-in-polygon, plus the four click scenarios (single atom, empty space, nearest resolution, hydrogen parity) — 14/14 green under xvfb. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp

findingGroups.title: Click-delete implementation
findings: Erase tool now offers two gestures: lasso group-delete and single-click single-atom delete, routed by the minimum-path guard at mouseReleaseEvent — a sub-threshold press-release clicks (deletes the nearest atom within pick radius via screen-space camera projection, no GL_SELECT), a longer drag lassos. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp handleClick/nearestAtomAt; erasetooltest testClickSingleAtom/testClickResolvesNearestAtom/testClickEmptySpace

Click and lasso deletions take the molecule write lock at release (tryLockForWrite) and abort cleanly on contention; a click is one DeleteAtomDrawCommand, a lasso is an UndoSequence of them, so each gesture is exactly one undo step with nothing mutated before release. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp mouseReleaseEvent; erasetooltest testSingleUndo

Managed-hydrogen parity with the Draw tool: with adjust-hydrogens on, a click/lasso deletes only heavy atoms and lets the delete churn managed hydrogens; with it off, enclosed/explicit hydrogens are deleted as victims, ordered first so undo restores the heavy atom before hydrogen bonds re-add. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp; erasetooltest testClickManagedHydrogenParity testManagedHydrogenParity

findingGroups.title: MSVC portability fix (caught by CI)
findings: The first Windows CI run failed to compile erasetooltest.cpp: `near` and `far` are MSVC far/near pointer-qualifier keywords, so `Atom *near`/`Atom *far` locals produced C2059. Renamed them to nearAtom/farAtom — a behavior-preserving rename; GCC treats them as ordinary identifiers. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp:358-361,379-380; confirmed by CI run 42356674345 passing where 42352599611 failed

findingGroups.title: Test coverage
findings: erasetooltest covers containment deletion, single-undo, managed-hydrogen parity, interrupted-lasso cleanup, lock-contention abort, overlay paint, point-in-polygon, plus the four click scenarios (single atom, empty space, nearest resolution, hydrogen parity) — 14/14 green under xvfb. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp

findingGroups.title: Click-delete implementation
findings: Erase tool now offers two gestures: lasso group-delete and single-click single-atom delete, routed by the minimum-path guard at mouseReleaseEvent — a sub-threshold press-release clicks (deletes the nearest atom within pick radius via screen-space camera projection, no GL_SELECT), a longer drag lassos. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp handleClick/nearestAtomAt; erasetooltest testClickSingleAtom/testClickResolvesNearestAtom/testClickEmptySpace

Click and lasso deletions take the molecule write lock at release (tryLockForWrite) and abort cleanly on contention; a click is one DeleteAtomDrawCommand, a lasso is an UndoSequence of them, so each gesture is exactly one undo step with nothing mutated before release. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp mouseReleaseEvent; erasetooltest testSingleUndo

Managed-hydrogen parity with the Draw tool: with adjust-hydrogens on, a click/lasso deletes only heavy atoms and lets the delete churn managed hydrogens; with it off, enclosed/explicit hydrogens are deleted as victims, ordered first so undo restores the heavy atom before hydrogen bonds re-add. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp; erasetooltest testClickManagedHydrogenParity testManagedHydrogenParity

findingGroups.title: MSVC portability fix (caught by CI)
findings: The first Windows CI run failed to compile erasetooltest.cpp: `near` and `far` are MSVC far/near pointer-qualifier keywords, so `Atom *near`/`Atom *far` locals produced C2059. findingGroups.title: Click-delete implementation
findings: Erase tool now offers two gestures: lasso group-delete and single-click single-atom delete, routed by the minimum-path guard at mouseReleaseEvent — a sub-threshold press-release clicks (deletes the nearest atom within pick radius via screen-space camera projection, no GL_SELECT), a longer drag lassos. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp handleClick/nearestAtomAt; erasetooltest testClickSingleAtom/testClickResolvesNearestAtom/testClickEmptySpace

Click and lasso deletions take the molecule write lock at release (tryLockForWrite) and abort cleanly on contention; a click is one DeleteAtomDrawCommand, a lasso is an UndoSequence of them, so each gesture is exactly one undo step with nothing mutated before release. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp mouseReleaseEvent; erasetooltest testSingleUndo

Managed-hydrogen parity with the Draw tool: with adjust-hydrogens on, a click/lasso deletes only heavy atoms and lets the delete churn managed hydrogens; with it off, enclosed/explicit hydrogens are deleted as victims, ordered first so undo restores the heavy atom before hydrogen bonds re-add. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp; erasetooltest testClickManagedHydrogenParity testManagedHydrogenParity

findingGroups.title: MSVC portability fix (caught by CI)
findings: The first Windows CI run failed to compile erasetooltest.cpp: `near` and `far` are MSVC far/near pointer-qualifier keywords, so `Atom *near`/`Atom *far` locals produced C2059. Renamed them to nearAtom/farAtom — a behavior-preserving rename; GCC treats them as ordinary identifiers. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp:358-361,379-380; confirmed by CI run 42356674345 passing where 42352599611 failed

findingGroups.title: Test coverage
findings: erasetooltest covers containment deletion, single-undo, managed-hydrogen parity, interrupted-lasso cleanup, lock-contention abort, overlay paint, point-in-polygon, plus the four click scenarios (single atom, empty space, nearest resolution, hydrogen parity) — 14/14 green under xvfb. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp

findingGroups.title: Click-delete implementation
findings: Erase tool now offers two gestures: lasso group-delete and single-click single-atom delete, routed by the minimum-path guard at mouseReleaseEvent — a sub-threshold press-release clicks (deletes the nearest atom within pick radius via screen-space camera projection, no GL_SELECT), a longer drag lassos. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp handleClick/nearestAtomAt; erasetooltest testClickSingleAtom/testClickResolvesNearestAtom/testClickEmptySpace

Click and lasso deletions take the molecule write lock at release (tryLockForWrite) and abort cleanly on contention; a click is one DeleteAtomDrawCommand, a lasso is an UndoSequence of them, so each gesture is exactly one undo step with nothing mutated before release. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp mouseReleaseEvent; erasetooltest testSingleUndo

Managed-hydrogen parity with the Draw tool: with adjust-hydrogens on, a click/lasso deletes only heavy atoms and lets the delete churn managed hydrogens; with it off, enclosed/explicit hydrogens are deleted as victims, ordered first so undo restores the heavy atom before hydrogen bonds re-add. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp; erasetooltest testClickManagedHydrogenParity testManagedHydrogenParity

findingGroups.title: MSVC portability fix (caught by CI)
findings: The first Windows CI run failed to compile erasetooltest.cpp: `near` and `far` are MSVC far/near pointer-qualifier keywords, so `Atom *near`/`Atom *far` locals produced C2059. Renamed them to nearAtom/farAtom — a behavior-preserving rename; GCC treats them as ordinary identifiers. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp:358-361,379-380; confirmed by CI run 42356674345 passing where 42352599611 failed

findingGroups.title: Test coverage
findings: erasetooltest covers containment deletion, single-undo, managed-hydrogen parity, interrupted-lasso cleanup, lock-contention abort, overlay paint, point-in-polygon, plus the four click scenarios (single atom, empty space, nearest resolution, hydrogen parity) — 14/14 green under xvfb. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Create `libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.h` / `erasetool.cpp`: `EraseTool : public Tool` with `AVOGADRO_TOOL("Erase", tr("Erase"), …)` metadata, constructor (eraser icon `:/erase/erase.png`, tooltip describing the lasso gesture, no keyboard shortcut), `usefulness()` just below Draw, and a `settingsWidget()` with an "Adjust Hydrogens" checkbox (default checked). Verify the tools plugin builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Implement `mousePressEvent`: record the press point in device pixels, begin a lasso gesture (clear the path, set dragging), lazily connect `toolActivated` (`Qt::UniqueConnection`) to abandon an in-flight loop on tool switch, accept the event. Verify it builds.
[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Implement `mouseMoveEvent`: while dragging, append the pointer position (device pixels) to the lasso path; accept. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 4] 1.4 Implement `mouseReleaseEvent` release assembly (D3/D4/D6/D10): apply the minimum-path guard (D4 — route a sub-threshold press-release to a click and a longer drag to a lasso), then acquire the molecule write lock with `tryLockForWrite` (D6 — abort cleanly on contention: discard polyline, no commands, no state), and on success assemble the deletion — a single `DeleteAtomDrawCommand` for a click (D10) or one command per victim inside an `UndoSequence` for a lasso (D3), text "Lasso Delete" — and return it. Verify it builds.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.1 Implement containment in device pixels: project every atom position through `widget->camera()->project()`, bbox-cull against the loop's bounding box, then even-odd point-in-polygon on the survivors; auto-close an unclosed path with a straight segment from end to start. Add a pure static helper `pointInPolygon` so it is unit-testable. Verify via the containment test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 6] 3.1 In the victim set, when adjust-hydrogens is enabled, exclude hydrogens from the victim set; heavy-atom victims pass `adjustHydrogens=true` to `DeleteAtomDrawCommand`. When disabled, every enclosed atom is a victim. Verify via the managed-hydrogen test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 7] 4.1 Implement `toolActivated(Tool*)` and the null-molecule / changed-document abandon: on tool switch, null molecule, or stale document, clear the lasso path and dragging flag (no command, no mutation); the next gesture starts clean. Verify via the interrupted-lasso test in 6.x.

[OpenSpec 8] 4.2 Implement `paint(GLWidget*)`: while dragging with a non-empty path, unproject the recorded device-pixel points to world space (at the widget-center depth) and draw a closed line loop via `widget->painter()->drawLineLoop(...)`, so the overlay renders on modern/compat/legacy tiers without "painter not active" diagnostics. Verify the overlay renders (run on a real window tier / check no diagnostic spam).

[OpenSpec 9] 5.1 Add the `erasetool` entry to `libavogadro/src/tools/CMakeLists.txt`, create `erasetool.qrc` referencing an eraser icon (`erase.png`), and verify the tool builds and appears in the palette: `cmake --build build --target erasetool`.

[OpenSpec 10] 6.1 Add `erasetooltest` to `libavogadro/tests/CMakeLists.txt` following the `selectionsettest`/`drawcommandtest` pattern (compiles `erasetool.cpp` + `drawcommand.cpp` directly, offscreen QPA, registered with ctest); verify it builds: `cmake --build build --target erasetooltest`.

[OpenSpec 11] 6.2 Implement the containment-deletion test: set up a molecule + GLWidget with a known camera, drive a lasso around a methyl group (and an unclosed loop), and assert enclosed atoms/bonds are deleted while outside atoms survive.
[OpenSpec 12] 6.3 Implement the tap no-op test: a press-and-release without significant travel deletes nothing and adds no undo entry.
[OpenSpec 13] 6.4 Implement the single-undo-step test: one undo restores the whole lasso (atoms + bonds), one redo re-deletes.

[OpenSpec 14] 6.5 Implement the managed-hydrogen parity test: with adjust-hydrogens on, looping a carbon deletes it and churns its managed hydrogens (not as independent victims); with it off, hydrogens are deleted as victims.
[OpenSpec 15] 6.6 Implement the interrupted-lasso cleanup test: tool switch mid-lasso (via `toolActivated`) leaves no residue and the next gesture starts clean.
[OpenSpec 16] 6.7 Run the new suite plus neighboring suites: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --test-dir build -R "erase|draw|molecule|selection" --output-on-failure` and confirm all green.

[OpenSpec 17] 7.1 Self-review the diff against design D1–D9 (containment space, guard semantics, undo grouping, hydrogen parity, lock discipline, overlay, gesture scoping, MSVC portability) and remove any throwaway artifacts.

[OpenSpec 18] 7.2 Trigger the Windows installer workflow (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) and verify the build and test suite pass on MSVC per repo policy before opening a PR. findingGroups.title: Click-delete implementation
findings: Erase tool now offers two gestures: lasso group-delete and single-click single-atom delete, routed by the minimum-path guard at mouseReleaseEvent — a sub-threshold press-release clicks (deletes the nearest atom within pick radius via screen-space camera projection, no GL_SELECT), a longer drag lassos. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp handleClick/nearestAtomAt; erasetooltest testClickSingleAtom/testClickResolvesNearestAtom/testClickEmptySpace

Click and lasso deletions take the molecule write lock at release (tryLockForWrite) and abort cleanly on contention; a click is one DeleteAtomDrawCommand, a lasso is an UndoSequence of them, so each gesture is exactly one undo step with nothing mutated before release. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp mouseReleaseEvent; erasetooltest testSingleUndo

Managed-hydrogen parity with the Draw tool: with adjust-hydrogens on, a click/lasso deletes only heavy atoms and lets the delete churn managed hydrogens; with it off, enclosed/explicit hydrogens are deleted as victims, ordered first so undo restores the heavy atom before hydrogen bonds re-add. — libavogadro/src/tools/erasetool.cpp; erasetooltest testClickManagedHydrogenParity testManagedHydrogenParity

findingGroups.title: MSVC portability fix (caught by CI)
findings: The first Windows CI run failed to compile erasetooltest.cpp: `near` and `far` are MSVC far/near pointer-qualifier keywords, so `Atom *near`/`Atom *far` locals produced C2059. Renamed them to nearAtom/farAtom — a behavior-preserving rename; GCC treats them as ordinary identifiers. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp:358-361,379-380; confirmed by CI run 42356674345 passing where 42352599611 failed

findingGroups.title: Test coverage
findings: erasetooltest covers containment deletion, single-undo, managed-hydrogen parity, interrupted-lasso cleanup, lock-contention abort, overlay paint, point-in-polygon, plus the four click scenarios (single atom, empty space, nearest resolution, hydrogen parity) — 14/14 green under xvfb. — libavogadro/tests/erasetooltest.cpp
